> **Notional system.** KESTREL is fictional. Its control selection uses NIST's published baselines as a stand-in, as Control Set explains.

# KESTREL Security Controls Traceability Matrix (SCTM)

*Generated by `tools/sctm/build.py` from the CCSD, the SADD, and the curated dispositions in `tools/sctm/dispositions.py`. Edit those, not this page.*

This matrix carries every control in KESTREL's approved set to the SADD outcomes that implement it, the providers it inherits from, and where its evidence is kept. The same rows are kept as OSCAL in KESTREL's system security plan, [`kestrel-ssp.oscal.json`](../06-ssp/kestrel-ssp.oscal.json), under SCTM Automation via Machine-Readable Format (OSCAL) (`GV-5.9.4`).

## Control Set

The CCSD selects KESTREL's controls from the CNSSI 1253 columns for High confidentiality, High integrity, and Moderate availability. This notional example does not reproduce those columns. It uses NIST's OSCAL [High baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_HIGH-baseline_profile.json) and [privacy baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_PRIVACY-baseline_profile.json) as a stand-in. The CCSD's tailoring actions then apply. SI-8 is removed with its enhancements, and SR-11(3) and SA-9(5) are added.

That gives 423 controls in the set. The cloud, OT, and IL5 overlays would add rows a real selection carries, and this stand-in omits them.

---

## How to Read Each Row

- **Control ID** and **Control Name** come from NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5.
- **Designation** is System-Specific when KESTREL implements the whole control, Inherited when a provider does, and Hybrid when both do.
- **Implementation Status** comes from the project board, through the SSP's status snapshot. A control is Planned until its outcomes' work starts reaching Done, Partially implemented once some has, and Implemented when every claiming outcome is done. A Hybrid control's status is KESTREL's own part, since the provider's part is already in place.
- **Narrative** says how KESTREL meets the control, naming the products and where they run, in future tense until the work is built. It then gives any provider's part and any CCSD tailoring. Its last sentence links to the part of the [SSP](../06-ssp/index.md) that tells the whole story, and each linked entry closes with its [Security Implementation Plan](../04-sip/index.md) record.
- **Evidence** for every row is kept in the program evidence repository under `evidence/<family>/<control>/`, under Compliance Evidence Collection and Retention (`CO-1.3`). Nothing is collected yet.

## Gaps for the SADD's Gap Register

These rows go to the SADD's gap register (Section 9) for disposition.

**Held but unclaimed (0).** An outcome already does this, or is where it belongs, but its mapping does not claim the control. Each needs a claim added to the outcome, or a recorded reason it stays unclaimed.

- None

**No owner (1).** No outcome or provider holds these.

- AC-18(5)

**Narrow owners (2).** These rest only on narrow outcomes. The SCTM does not read them as system-wide, and each still needs a system-wide owner named.

- CM-6(2): DI-4.1, AI-4.18, AI-9.3 (Partial)
- SA-5: AI-5.8, AI-6.2 (Partial)

## Matrix

### AC: Access Control

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the access control policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Account Management Plan (AMP) will hold the procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [ID-5.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-51-account-management-plan-amp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| AC-2 | Account Management | System-Specific | Planned | Accounts will be managed through one lifecycle. Active Directory in the mission data center holds every account, with Entra ID as its cloud copy. Access is granted in role bundles scoped by team. IT Operations changes group membership only through a recorded Jira Service Management request, which the requester's team lead approves. Partner and vendor accounts are tied to a sponsor and to their support cases or partner API roles. Access is recertified on the AMP's cadence. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship), [ID-1.3](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-13-centralized-identity-platform), [ID-1.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-17-identities-and-entitlements-lifecycle), [ID-1.9](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-19-access-reviews), [ID-1.10](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-110-physical-and-logical-access-convergence). |
| AC-2(1) | Account Management \| Automated System Account Management | System-Specific | Planned | Account management will be automated. Entra ID Governance creates the baseline account when enrollment completes, and accounts are synchronized continuously against the authoritative source. Splunk computes dormancy each day, and Ansible disables any account dormant past the AMP's threshold. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment), [ID-1.8](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-18-account-lifecycle-and-identity-data-quality). |
| AC-2(2) | Account Management \| Automated Temporary and Emergency Account Management | System-Specific | Planned | Temporary and emergency accounts will be controlled automatically. Maintenance access to the fleet opens only for a scheduled window. Vendor sessions end when their case closes, after eight hours at most. Break-glass sessions end after four hours, or once no aircraft under a station is airborne. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-45-otlegacy-scheduled-maintenance-window-access), [ID-4.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-46-emergency-access), [ID-4.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-47-access-process-for-third-party-support). |
| AC-2(3) | Account Management \| Disable Accounts | System-Specific | Planned | Accounts will be disabled when they are no longer needed. A departure disables the person's Active Directory account and revokes their CAC binding, and accounts dormant past the AMP's threshold are disabled automatically. Each service account has a named owner and is removed when its service is. During an incident, a compromised account can be disabled at once. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.8](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-18-account-lifecycle-and-identity-data-quality), [ID-3.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-32-application-and-service-account-identities), [RS-3.2](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-32-automated-containment-and-isolation-procedures). |
| AC-2(4) | Account Management \| Automated Audit Actions | System-Specific | Planned | Every account creation, change, disable, and removal will be logged to Splunk from the directory and from Entra ID. The SSP describes it under [DE-2.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-21-infrastructure-and-identity-logging). |
| AC-2(5) | Account Management \| Inactivity Logout | System-Specific | Planned | Cloud and VDI sessions will end after the AMP's inactivity limit. Ground control stations are the exception while their aircraft is airborne, since a logged-out operator could endanger the flight. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-26-continuous-authentication). |
| AC-2(11) | Account Management \| Usage Conditions | System-Specific | Planned | Conditional Access will set the conditions on each account's use, such as device compliance and network origin. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-25-adaptive-risk-based-access-control). |
| AC-2(12) | Account Management \| Account Monitoring for Atypical Usage | System-Specific | Planned | Accounts will be monitored for atypical use. Splunk Enterprise Security baselines each role's behavior and flags deviations, such as bulk reads across data lake zones. Any use of a break-glass account alerts the Security Team and the CSSP. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-46-emergency-access), [DA-1.5](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-15-data-loss-prevention-dlp-and-monitoring), [DE-1.6](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-16-userentity-behavior-analytics-ueba--insider-threat-detection). |
| AC-2(13) | Account Management \| Disable Accounts for High-risk Individuals | System-Specific | Planned | The account of anyone posing a significant risk will be disabled at once through Entra ID and Defender XDR, revoking their sessions, under the IRP. The SSP describes it under [RS-3.2](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-32-automated-containment-and-isolation-procedures). |
| AC-3 | Access Enforcement | System-Specific | Planned | Access will be enforced by the identity provider and by an attribute-based policy. Roles are Active Directory groups scoped by team, so an analyst cannot reach another team's payload vendor data. An OPA policy decision service decides data access from the user's attributes and each record's labels. Retrieval for the LLM analyst assistant enforces the requesting user's entitlements, and each agent's memory is scoped per repository or per user. The SSP describes them under [ID-2.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-24-non-privileged-access-control), [AI-3.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-34-training-script-and-feature-engineering-ip-protection), [AI-8.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-84-retrieval-augmented-generation-rag-and-vector-store-security), [AI-8.15](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-815-agent-memory-security). |

The SSP describes it under [CO-4.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-41-privacy-program-management). |
| AC-4 | Information Flow Enforcement | System-Specific | Planned | Information flows will be enforced at every boundary. Workload security groups, ACI contracts, and Cilium network policies allow only each team's mapped flows, and the ground segment's conduits allow only approved traffic. Data loss prevention sits on every outbound path, and the partner API and the cross domain gateway check every release against its markings. Each agent tool call is checked against what its task authorized. The SSP describes them under [NE-1.5](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-15-network-micro-segmentation), [NE-1.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-16-itot-zone-and-conduit-segmentation-iec-62443), [AP-2.17](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-217-network-policy-verification), [AI-8.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-87-agentic-tool-callaction-output-validation), [DA-1.5](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-15-data-loss-prevention-dlp-and-monitoring). |
| AC-4(4) | Information Flow Enforcement \| Flow Control of Encrypted Information | System-Specific | Planned | Both hubs will decrypt outbound TLS so its content can be inspected. | AC-5 | Separation of Duties | System-Specific | Planned | Duties will be separated where combining them would let one person cause harm alone. No merge is approved by its own author. Phishing exercises come from the parent organization's and the performer's email programs. The SSP describes it under [GV-2.3](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-23-security-awareness-and-training-program). |
| AT-3 | Role-based Training | Hybrid | Planned | Role-based training will add courses for the roles with the most consequence. These are operators, OT maintainers, the staff who receive hardware, incident responders, and everyone with a contingency role. Each course is taken before the role starts and each year after. **Inherited from DoD enterprise services:** DoD role-based training content on JKO. The SSP describes it under [GV-2.3](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-23-security-awareness-and-training-program). |
| AT-3(5) | Role-based Training \| Processing Personally Identifiable Information | System-Specific | Planned | Staff who handle personal information will be trained on how to process it, under the privacy program. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-41-privacy-program-management). |
| AT-4 | Training Records | System-Specific | Planned | Training completion will be recorded per user, and the record drives the account disable when a course lapses. Records are kept with the user's account records. The SSP describes it under [GV-2.3](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-23-security-awareness-and-training-program). |

### AU: Audit and Accountability

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AU-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the audit and accountability policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Security Team's logging procedures will carry it out. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DE-2.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-21-infrastructure-and-identity-logging), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| AU-2 | Event Logging | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will log the events that matter to its security. These include sign-ins and their risk, access decisions, privileged actions, configuration changes, data access and export, release events, agent tool calls, and the events from every security tool. The Security Team confirms each event class is present and reviews the list each year. The SSP describes it under [DE-1.8](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-18-identity-threat-detection). |
| AU-3 | Content of Audit Records | System-Specific | Planned | Each audit record will say what happened, when and where, its source, its outcome, and the identity behind it. A shared logging library gives each team's application the same record structure, and COTS output is normalized when it reaches Splunk. The SSP describes it under [DE-2.4](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-24-applicationapi-logging). |
| AU-3(1) | Content of Audit Records \| Additional Audit Information | System-Specific | Planned | Records will carry the extra detail each source class needs. Examples are the parameters and approval of each agent tool call, and the object and partner behind each data release. The SSP describes it under [DE-2.4](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-24-applicationapi-logging). |
| AU-3(3) | Content of Audit Records \| Limit Personally Identifiable Information Elements | System-Specific | Planned | Application logs will limit the personal information they record to what an investigation needs, and Presidio redacts personal information from inference logs. The SSP describes it under [DE-2.4](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-24-applicationapi-logging). |
| AU-4 | Audit Log Storage Capacity | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk will be sized to hold 12 months of searchable security logs, with StorageGRID holding 18 more. The Security Team monitors capacity, and storage warnings reach the logging administrators before space runs out. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.2](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-32-log-retention-strategy). |
| AU-5 | Response to Audit Logging Process Failures | System-Specific | Planned | A failure in logging will alert the Security Team. Splunk tracks every source's expected volume, and a source that goes silent or a pipeline that stops raises an alert. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.3](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-33-audit-log-integrity-protection). |
| AU-5(1) | Response to Audit Logging Process Failures \| Storage Capacity Warning | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk will warn the logging administrators when its storage approaches a set threshold, in time to add capacity before records are lost. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.3](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-33-audit-log-integrity-protection). |
| AU-5(2) | Response to Audit Logging Process Failures \| Real-time Alerts | System-Specific | Planned | A silent log source will raise a real-time alert within the hour, so a gap in logging is caught quickly. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.3](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-33-audit-log-integrity-protection). |
| AU-6 | Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting | Hybrid | Planned | The Security Team will review and analyze audit records in Splunk Enterprise Security, and report findings to the ISSM. The CSSP monitors the same telemetry around the clock under its service agreement, reading it through its own host pool. **Inherited from the CSSP:** Review and analysis of forwarded telemetry. The SSP describes them under [DE-1.8](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-18-identity-threat-detection), [DE-3.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-31-siem-capabilities). |
| AU-6(1) | Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting \| Automated Process Integration | System-Specific | Planned | Review, analysis, and reporting will be integrated with response. Splunk SOAR enriches each alert, opens its ticket, and notifies the right people, so review flows directly into incident handling. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-31-siem-capabilities). |
| AU-6(3) | Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting \| Correlate Audit Record Repositories | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk will correlate records across every repository, from the cloud and the data center to the alternate site and the ground segment. One event can then be followed across all of them. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-31-siem-capabilities). |
| AU-6(5) | Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting \| Integrated Analysis of Audit Records | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk will analyze audit records together with vulnerability scan results, performance data, and other monitoring, so a detection draws on all of them at once. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-31-siem-capabilities). |
| AU-6(6) | Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting \| Correlation with Physical Monitoring | System-Specific | Planned | Badge events from the physical access control systems will be correlated with sign-ins. An operator signed in at a station without having badged into that site raises an alert. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.10](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-110-physical-and-logical-access-convergence). |
| AU-7 | Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk will reduce and report on audit records on demand, with searches, dashboards, and reports that leave the original records unchanged. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-31-siem-capabilities). |
| AU-7(1) | Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation \| Automatic Processing | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk will process audit records automatically, filtering and correlating them by the fields an analyst chooses, such as user, asset, or time window. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-31-siem-capabilities). |
| AU-8 | Time Stamps | System-Specific | Planned | Every record will carry a time stamp from a shared reference. On-premises hosts take time from GNSS-disciplined SyncServer time servers, checked against DoD's authoritative time service, and cloud workloads use the provider's time service. Splunk alerts on drift between the two. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.4](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-34-time-synchronization). |
| AU-9 | Protection of Audit Information | System-Specific | Planned | Audit records will be protected from change and deletion. Splunk writes each record to a StorageGRID bucket under S3 Object Lock in compliance mode, and no role holds the capability to delete logs. Break-glass access through CyberArk raises an alert. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.3](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-33-audit-log-integrity-protection). |
| AU-9(2) | Protection of Audit Information \| Store on Separate Physical Systems or Components | System-Specific | Planned | Audit records will be stored on a separate system from the components they describe. Splunk and its StorageGRID archive sit apart from the systems being logged, and all telemetry is also forwarded to the CSSP. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.3](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-33-audit-log-integrity-protection). |
| AU-9(3) | Protection of Audit Information \| Cryptographic Protection | System-Specific | Planned | Audit records will be protected cryptographically. Splunk hashes each batch it writes, GitLab's audit stream is hashed in batches, and the provenance ledger's entries are hash-chained and signed, so any alteration is detectable. The SSP describes them under [AP-4.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-43-approver-and-reviewer-audit-log), [AI-4.16](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-416-training-job-audit-logging), [DA-1.3](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-13-data-provenance-and-lineage-verification), [DE-3.3](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-33-audit-log-integrity-protection). |
| AU-9(4) | Protection of Audit Information \| Access by Subset of Privileged Users | System-Specific | Planned | Only named Security Team members will hold the logging administrator role. Platform Team administrators cannot change the audit records of the systems they run. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.3](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-33-audit-log-integrity-protection). |
| AU-10 | Non-repudiation | System-Specific | Planned | Actions will be bound to the people behind them. Each AI agent action records the principal who invoked it, so no one can deny an action taken on their behalf. Incident evidence is tracked through its collection, access, transfer, and release, so no one who handled an item can deny it. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.3](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-33-ai-agent-identities), [RS-2.3](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-23-evidence-preservation-and-forensic-capabilities). |
| AU-11 | Audit Record Retention | System-Specific | Planned | Security logs will be kept searchable for 12 months and archived for 18 more, 30 months in all. Alert and investigation records are kept for 3 years, and longer where a case or POA&M item requires it. Incident evidence follows the IRP's retention terms. The SSP describes it under [DE-3.2](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-32-log-retention-strategy). |
| AU-12 | Audit Record Generation | System-Specific | Planned | Every component will generate audit records, with logging turned on when it is created. Cloud resources log through Azure Monitor diagnostic settings, and on-premises systems through Splunk forwarders. Applications log through the shared library, and the ground segment through the IT/OT DMZ. Azure Policy and a Splunk source check flag any component missing its logging. The SSP describes them under [AP-4.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-43-approver-and-reviewer-audit-log), [AI-4.16](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-416-training-job-audit-logging), [AI-6.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-64-risk-acceptance-and-approval-log), [DA-2.3](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-23-secure-file-transfer-and-management-protocols), [DE-2.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-21-infrastructure-and-identity-logging), [DE-2.2](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-22-data-service-logging), [DE-2.3](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-23-container-and-orchestration-platform-logging), [DE-2.4](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-24-applicationapi-logging), [DE-2.5](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-25-host-and-endpoint-logging), [DE-2.6](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-26-edge-attack-surface-logging), [DE-2.7](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-27-network-security-logging), [DE-2.8](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-28-otlegacy-telemetry-ingestion-and-normalization). |
| AU-12(1) | Audit Record Generation \| System-wide and Time-correlated Audit Trail | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk will assemble a system-wide audit trail, ordered by the shared time reference, and stitch each connection together across the circuits. The SSP describes them under [DE-3.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-31-siem-capabilities), [DE-3.4](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-34-time-synchronization). |
| AU-12(3) | Audit Record Generation \| Changes by Authorized Individuals | System-Specific | Planned | During an investigation, authorized Security Team members will be able to change which events a component logs, or raise its detail, without stopping it. Each such change is itself recorded. The SSP describes it under [RS-2.2](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-22-incident-scoped-log-analysis-and-investigation). |

### CA: Assessment, Authorization, and Monitoring

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CA-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Continuous Monitoring Plan will hold the procedures. The AO approves the Continuous Monitoring Plan, and both are reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework), [CO-2.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-21-continuous-monitoring-plan-conmon). |
| CA-2 | Control Assessments | System-Specific | Planned | The SCA will assess KESTREL's controls under a Security Assessment Plan written from the SCTM, starting on 2028-07-31. The assessment covers the cloud, the data center, the alternate site, the fleet through spares and the simulator, and each model through its evidence annex. Inherited controls are assessed by reviewing each provider's package. After authorization, controls are reassessed on the Continuous Monitoring Plan's calendar. The SSP describes them under [RK-1.5](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-15-security-assessment-plan), [RK-1.6](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-16-security-assessment-report-sar), [CO-2.2](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-22-control-assessment-scheduling), [CO-2.3](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-23-annual-security-review). |
| CA-2(1) | Control Assessments \| Independent Assessors | System-Specific | Planned | Assessments will be performed by the SCA, who is independent of the teams that build and run KESTREL. The SSP describes it under [CO-2.2](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-22-control-assessment-scheduling). |
| CA-2(2) | Control Assessments \| Specialized Assessments | System-Specific | Planned | Specialized assessments will add depth where it matters: penetration testing each year, AI red teaming of each new use case, and adversary emulation from Phase 4. The SSP describes it under [CO-2.3](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-23-annual-security-review). |
| CA-3 | Information Exchange | System-Specific | Planned | Each information exchange with an outside system will rest on a signed agreement, stored in Confluence and recorded in eMASS. The CSSP and access point agreements are signed in Phase 1, and partner nation agreements before each partner's first release. Each is reviewed every year and whenever its connection changes. The SSP describes it under [GV-5.6](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-56-system-interconnection-agreements-isamoumoa). |
| CA-3(6) | Information Exchange \| Transfer Authorizations | System-Specific | Planned | Each transfer across the cross domain solution will be authorized. Low-to-high baselines need Certification to Field approval before they are staged, and high-to-low products need the IL6 enclave's release review. The interconnection agreements authorize each type of transfer. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.10](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-210-cross-domain-solution-cds-transfer-procedures). |
| CA-5 | Plan of Action and Milestones | System-Specific | Planned | POA&M items will live in eMASS from Phase 1, covering the conditions of the interim authorization to test, assessment findings, missed remediation deadlines, and open STIG findings. Milestones are reviewed each month and reported to the AO each quarter, and an ISSO closes an item only after verifying the fix. The SSP describes them under [AP-5.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-52-stig-risk-tracking), [RK-1.8](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-18-plan-of-action-and-milestones-poam). |
| CA-6 | Authorization | System-Specific | Planned | The AO will grant an interim authorization to test in Phase 1. It covers the spare aircraft and the simulator, the access point and CSSP connections, and the prior collection. The ATO decision is due on 2028-09-30, on the full package the ISSM submits in eMASS. After that, the authorization is kept current through ongoing authorization, with agreed reauthorization triggers and a status report to the AO each quarter. The SSP describes them under [GV-5.7](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-57-authorization-to-operate-ato-process), [GV-5.10](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-510-ongoing-authorization). |
| CA-7 | Continuous Monitoring | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will be monitored continuously under the Continuous Monitoring Plan. Each check has a frequency and an owner, and its results reach the Splunk posture dashboard and eMASS. The checks range from account reconciliation, vulnerability and application findings, and backup health to model drift and re-testing. The ISSM reports to the AO each quarter. The SSP describes them under [ID-5.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-52-amp-compliance-verification), [AP-5.6](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-56-unified-vulnerability-dashboard), [AI-9.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-91-model-drift-detection-and-alerting), [AI-9.9](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-99-operational-adversarial-re-testing), [RC-1.6](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-16-backup-health-and-operations-monitoring), [CO-2.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-21-continuous-monitoring-plan-conmon). |
| CA-7(1) | Continuous Monitoring \| Independent Assessment | System-Specific | Planned | The SCA will perform the independent portion of continuous monitoring, reassessing controls on the calendar the Continuous Monitoring Plan sets. The SSP describes it under [CO-2.2](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-22-control-assessment-scheduling). |
| CA-7(4) | Continuous Monitoring \| Risk Monitoring | System-Specific | Planned | Risk monitoring will cover accepted risks as well as open findings. Accepted design risks and risk acceptances carry review dates, and the steering committee reviews the risk register each month. The SSP describes it under [AP-5.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-51-architecture-risk-tracking). |
| CA-8 | Penetration Testing | System-Specific | Planned | Independent penetration testers will test all of KESTREL each year, and the paths reachable from outside every six months, starting in Phase 2. They also test after a major change. Fleet systems are tested on spares or the simulator, and each finding becomes a POA&M item retested before it closes. The SSP describes it under [AP-3.5](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-35-penetration-testing). |
| CA-8(1) | Penetration Testing \| Independent Penetration Testing Agent or Team | System-Specific | Planned | The penetration testing provider will be independent of the performer, under its own contract and rules of engagement. The ISSM scopes each test, so the people who designed a control do not scope its check. The SSP describes it under [AP-3.5](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-35-penetration-testing). |
| CA-9 | Internal System Connections | System-Specific | Planned | Internal connections between KESTREL's components will be documented and reviewed. Managed services connect only inside their spoke's subnets, through the hub's routes and inspection. Each quarter, the Platform Team removes any internal connection that no longer matches a documented flow. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.2](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-22-platform-service-network-integration). |

### CM: Configuration Management

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CM-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the configuration management policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Configuration Management Plan (CMP) will hold the procedures that carry it out. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DI-6.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-61-configuration-management-plan-cmp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| CM-2 | Baseline Configuration | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL's baselines will come from DISA STIGs and SRGs, with the Cloud Computing SRG's IL5 requirements in the cloud. They are held as code. Landing zone modules define the cloud's hub and spokes, and Packer images define servers and VDI desktops. Containers start from Iron Bank base images, managed services follow Azure Policy initiatives, and Ansible roles carry the baselines on premises. Fleet equipment follows each manufacturer's hardening guidance, and each release carries a versioned runtime baseline. The SSP describes them under [DI-3.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-31-secure-configurations), [DI-3.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-32-secure-compute-baselines), [DI-3.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-33-secure-storage-baselines), [DI-3.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-34-secure-platform-services-and-application-baselines), [DI-3.5](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-35-secure-otlegacy-device-baselines), [NE-1.1](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-11-network-centralization-and-standardization), [AP-4.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-44-runtime-security-baseline). |
| CM-2(2) | Baseline Configuration \| Automation Support for Accuracy and Currency | System-Specific | Planned | Baselines will be kept current and accurate by the same automation that applies them. The landing zone modules, Packer images, and Ansible roles live in GitLab. A change to a baseline is therefore a reviewed merge request, and every new build picks it up. Training environments pin their dependencies and image digests, and each run checks its environment against the approved baseline before it starts. System prompts are versioned with each release in the same way. The SSP describes them under [DI-3.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-31-secure-configurations), [AI-3.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-32-experiment-tracking-and-reproducibility), [AI-4.13](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-413-reproducibility-controls), [AI-8.10](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-810-system-prompt-governance). |
| CM-2(3) | Baseline Configuration \| Retention of Previous Configurations | System-Specific | Planned | Previous configurations will be kept so a change can be rolled back. GitLab keeps the full history of every baseline and policy as code. Artifactory keeps every fielded release and the certified release before it, and the model registry keeps each model's prior certified version. Backups keep each system's configuration as part of its tier's backup policy. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.8](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-48-vulnerability-and-patch-management), [AP-5.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-54-registry-hygiene-report), [AI-9.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-97-model-registry-hygiene-report), [RC-1.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-14-otlegacy-configuration-and-engineering-backup). |
| CM-2(7) | Baseline Configuration \| Configure Systems and Components for High-risk Areas | System-Specific | Planned | The privileged access workstations are KESTREL's only endpoints that stay outside the VDI pools, and none of them travels. They are enrolled in Configuration Manager in the Tier 0 enclave and held to a dedicated compliance policy. KESTREL has no mobile devices, so no travel configuration is needed. The SSP describes it under [DI-4.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-41-device-compliance). |
| CM-3 | Configuration Change Control | System-Specific | Planned | Every change will have a change record. For anything defined as code, that is the merged GitLab merge request, approved by a second reviewer. Jira Service Management holds the record for everything else, including fleet changes. System prompts change only through the pipeline, reviewed like code. Changes to the shared firewall rule base, the identity provider, or an interconnection go to the Configuration Control Board, which the chief engineer chairs. Emergency changes run through CyberArk and are reviewed within two business days. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-22-asset-lifecycle-change-control), [NE-1.1](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-11-network-centralization-and-standardization), [AI-8.10](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-810-system-prompt-governance), [GV-1.5](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-15-configuration-control-board). |
| CM-3(1) | Configuration Change Control \| Automated Documentation, Notification, and Prohibition of Changes | System-Specific | Planned | GitLab will enforce change control automatically. Protected branches block a merge until its required approvals and checks pass. Code owners mark sensitive paths, such as pipeline definitions, infrastructure as code, admission policy, and agent configuration. A change to one needs extra approval and raises an alert in Splunk. Open Policy Agent rejects changes that break policy in the pipeline and at cluster admission. Privileged changes to training configuration alert the ML Team and the Security Team. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.18](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-218-pre-merge-sensitive-repo-file-change-detection), [AP-2.19](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-219-policy-as-code-evaluation), [AI-4.17](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-417-privileged-config-change-alerting). |
| CM-3(2) | Configuration Change Control \| Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes | System-Specific | Planned | Changes will be tested before they reach production. Cloud changes go first to the owning team's stage cluster. Tier 0 and data center changes go to the alternate site's standby or a lab, and a change with neither records an exception and gets extra checking afterward. A compliance scan after the change closes its record. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-22-asset-lifecycle-change-control). |
| CM-3(4) | Configuration Change Control \| Security and Privacy Representatives | System-Specific | Planned | Security sits on the change path itself. A change to a sensitive repository path needs the Platform Team's and the Security Team's approval beyond the team's own reviewer. The PMO ISSE and the ISSM are members of the Configuration Control Board. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.18](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-218-pre-merge-sensitive-repo-file-change-detection), [AI-4.17](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-417-privileged-config-change-alerting). |
| CM-3(6) | Configuration Change Control \| Cryptography Management | System-Specific | Planned | Changes to cryptographic mechanisms, such as algorithms, key lengths, and certificate profiles, will go through the Key Management Plan and the Configuration Control Board. The SSP describes it under [DA-3.13](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-313-key-management-plan-kmp). |
| CM-4 | Impact Analyses | System-Specific | Planned | Each change will carry a security impact note, answering what it touches, whether it changes a boundary or an identity's access, and which controls it affects. Every note feeds a Security Impact Analysis, which the ISSM runs against what the authorization was granted on. A significant change goes to the SCA and the AO before it is made. A change to a system prompt's role or limits also triggers jailbreak and injection testing. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-22-asset-lifecycle-change-control), [AI-8.10](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-810-system-prompt-governance), [GV-5.11](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-511-security-impact-analysis-sia). |
| CM-4(1) | Impact Analyses \| Separate Test Environments | System-Specific | Planned | Changes will be analyzed in separate environments before production. Each team has its own dev, test, and stage clusters, with stage carrying production's configuration. On-premises and Tier 0 changes are tried on the alternate site's standby or in a lab. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-22-asset-lifecycle-change-control). |
| CM-4(2) | Impact Analyses \| Verification of Controls | System-Specific | Planned | After a change is made, the controls its impact analysis identified will be checked again. The check confirms each control is implemented correctly, operating as intended, and meeting its requirements. The results are recorded on the Security Impact Analysis record. The SSP describes it under [GV-5.11](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-511-security-impact-analysis-sia). |
| CM-5 | Access Restrictions for Change | System-Specific | Planned | Only approved people and pipelines will be able to change production. Each team's pipeline identity reaches only its own repositories and dev/test spoke. Only the release identity, on a separate protected runner, can deploy to production, and it is unlocked only by Certification to Field's approval. Protected branches require a second reviewer and signed commits, with no administrator bypass. Training identities write only to their own run's output. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.22](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-222-least-privilege-cibuild-infrastructure-access), [AP-4.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-41-branch-protection-policy-report), [AP-4.6](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-46-application-rollback-progressive-delivery-and-feature-flag-governance), [AI-4.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-42-least-privilege-training-infrastructure-access). |
| CM-5(1) | Access Restrictions for Change \| Automated Access Enforcement and Audit Records | System-Specific | Planned | GitLab will enforce those restrictions and record each one. Every review, approval, dismissal, and override streams to Splunk, where Platform Team administrators cannot change it. Each approval is checked against the approver's entitlement in Entra ID Governance at the time it was given. The SSP describes them under [AP-4.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-41-branch-protection-policy-report), [AP-4.6](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-46-application-rollback-progressive-delivery-and-feature-flag-governance). |
| CM-6 | Configuration Settings | System-Specific | Planned | Each class of asset will be configured to its baseline's settings. Domain controllers, certificate authorities, and sync servers follow their DISA STIGs. Containers must run as non-root with a read-only filesystem, dropped capabilities, and resource limits. Fleet equipment follows its manufacturer's hardening guide. Each deviation from a STIG is recorded with its reason and approved through change control. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-14-identity-platform-threat-detection-and-hardening), [ID-1.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-15-directory-and-tier-0-infrastructure-hardening), [DI-3.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-32-secure-compute-baselines), [DI-4.7](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-47-ot-baseline-configuration-drift-detection), [NE-1.2](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-12-network-infrastructure-device-hardening), [AP-2.16](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-216-container-hardening-verification), [AP-3.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-33-application-security-and-development-asd-stig-compliance). |
| CM-6(1) | Configuration Settings \| Automated Management, Application, and Verification | System-Specific | Planned | Settings will be applied and checked automatically. OpenTofu and Ansible apply them, Azure Policy and Conftest check infrastructure as code before it deploys, and Gatekeeper rejects non-compliant workloads at admission. Azure Machine Configuration, Defender for Cloud CSPM, and ACAS STIG audits then check running systems continuously, and results feed compliance dashboards in Splunk. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-21-secure-resource-provisioning), [DI-4.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-41-device-compliance), [DI-4.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-44-compute-configuration-monitoring), [DI-4.5](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-45-storage-configuration-monitoring), [DI-4.6](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-46-platform-services-and-application-configuration-monitoring), [NE-1.1](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-11-network-centralization-and-standardization), [AP-2.15](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-215-iac-scanning), [AP-2.16](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-216-container-hardening-verification), [AP-3.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-33-application-security-and-development-asd-stig-compliance), [AP-4.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-44-runtime-security-baseline), [AI-4.8](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-48-training-infrastructure-iac-scanning), [AI-4.18](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-418-hyperparameter-change-alerting). |
| CM-6(2) | Configuration Settings \| Respond to Unauthorized Changes | System-Specific | Planned | When an unauthorized change is found, KESTREL will respond automatically where it can do so safely. A privileged access workstation that drifts loses Tier 0 sign-in until Configuration Manager restores it. A change to a training hyperparameter outside its approved range alerts the ML Team, and a retraining pipeline that fails its integrity check halts. Firewall policy that drifts from its repository is reverted within one business day. A system-wide owner is still to be named, and it is tracked as a gap. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-41-device-compliance), [AI-4.18](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-418-hyperparameter-change-alerting), [AI-9.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-93-retraining-pipeline-integrity-verification). |
| CM-7 | Least Functionality | System-Specific | Planned | Every asset will run only the services its function needs. Images are built minimal, managed services expose only private endpoints, and the CMP lists the ports, protocols, and services each asset type may use. Host firewalls and the shared firewall rule base deny everything else. The SSP describes them under [DI-3.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-32-secure-compute-baselines), [DI-3.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-34-secure-platform-services-and-application-baselines), [DI-4.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-42-policy-service-restrictions), [NE-2.2](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-22-platform-service-network-integration), [NE-2.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-27-secure-remote-access). |
| CM-7(1) | Least Functionality \| Periodic Review | System-Specific | Planned | Running services will be reviewed against the permitted list. ACAS scans and Defender for Cloud CSPM look for services outside the CMP's list. Network flows and firewall rules are reviewed against the approved flow map, and API Management reports any API endpoint that answers but was never registered. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-43-unapproved-service-usage-monitoring-and-alerting), [NE-1.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-13-insecure-services-and-protocols), [NE-2.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-26-web-application-firewall), [AP-5.7](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-57-runtime-api-inventory-and-governance). |
| CM-7(2) | Least Functionality \| Prevent Program Execution | System-Specific | Planned | App Control for Business on Windows and fapolicyd on Red Hat Enterprise Linux will block any program that is not on the allow-list. They run in audit mode during Phase 2 and enforce by Phase 3. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| CM-7(5) | Least Functionality \| Authorized Software — Allow-by-exception | System-Specific | Planned | Software will run by exception only. The allow-lists name the programs each class of host may run, and everything else is denied. To add a program, a team asks through Jira Service Management and the Security Team reviews the request. The Platform Team then adds it to the signed policy through a merge request. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| CM-8 | System Component Inventory | System-Specific | Planned | Jira Service Management Assets will be KESTREL's one inventory. Azure Resource Graph feeds it for the cloud, Defender for Endpoint for on-premises hosts, and the Cisco APIC for the data center network. Passive sensors and Fleet Operations' records feed the fleet. Each application and each certified model version is registered too, and so are third-party products once their supplier assessment passes. The SSP describes them under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery), [DI-1.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-12-otlegacy-passive-protocol-aware-discovery), [DI-2.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-23-resource-decommissioning-governance), [AP-4.7](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-47-application-registration-and-inventory-logging), [AI-6.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-67-model-registration-and-inventory-logging), [GV-3.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-31-vendor-security-risk-assessment), [GV-4.6](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-46-aiml-vendormodel-risk-assessment). |
| CM-8(1) | System Component Inventory \| Updates During Installation and Removal | System-Specific | Planned | The inventory will change when components do. Provisioning and decommissioning update it as part of the same change, and a deployment to production fails unless its application is registered. Each certified model version is registered when it is certified. The SSP describes them under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery), [AP-4.7](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-47-application-registration-and-inventory-logging), [AI-6.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-67-model-registration-and-inventory-logging). |
| CM-8(2) | System Component Inventory \| Automated Maintenance | System-Specific | Planned | The inventory will be maintained automatically from the cloud's resource inventory, the endpoint agents, and the SDN controller. A deployment inventory in Splunk compares what is running with what was certified, and the model registry reports its own state each month. The SSP describes them under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery), [AP-5.5](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-55-deployment-inventory-report), [AI-9.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-97-model-registry-hygiene-report). |
| CM-8(3) | System Component Inventory \| Automated Unauthorized Component Detection | System-Specific | Planned | Unauthorized components will be detected automatically. A subscription created outside the landing zone alerts, and so does a device the Cisco APIC does not recognize. Passive sensors flag unknown devices on the ground segment. Anything running in production that was never certified is flagged, and the model registry admits only models from approved sources. The SSP describes them under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery), [DI-1.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-12-otlegacy-passive-protocol-aware-discovery), [AP-5.5](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-55-deployment-inventory-report), [AI-9.6](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-96-trusted-model-registry-source-validation). |
| CM-8(4) | System Component Inventory \| Accountability Information | System-Specific | Planned | Every asset will carry tags naming its owning team, segment, environment, data classification, mission criticality, and end-of-support date. The pipeline rejects an untagged cloud resource, and Fleet Operations tags fleet equipment when it is received. The SSP describes it under [DI-1.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-13-resource-tagging-and-ownership-strategy). |
| CM-9 | Configuration Management Plan | System-Specific | Planned | The Platform Team will write the Configuration Management Plan, with Fleet Operations writing the OT and legacy sections and IT Operations the maintenance sections. The Security Team reviews it, and the Configuration Control Board approves it. It is revised each year and after any significant change, such as a new spoke or interconnection. The SSP describes it under [DI-6.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-61-configuration-management-plan-cmp). |
| CM-10 | Software Usage Restrictions | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will track the license terms of every licensed product, including the foundation model's terms, in Jira Service Management Assets. Peer-to-peer file sharing software is prohibited. The SSP describes it under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery). |
| CM-11 | User-installed Software | System-Specific | Planned | Users will not be able to install software. Allow-listing on every host blocks anything not on the approved list, and new software reaches a host only through the request and merge process described for CM-7(5). The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| CM-12 | Information Location | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will know where its information lives. The Data Team labels every record at ingest, and OpenMetadata catalogs every data store and classifies databases and structured files by their content. The catalog is checked against the CCSD's information types. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.1](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-11-data-discovery-labeling-and-classification). |
| CM-12(1) | Information Location \| Automated Tools to Support Information Location | System-Specific | Planned | OpenMetadata will scan the data stores automatically over a read-only identity, so the record of where information lives stays current without manual surveys. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.1](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-11-data-discovery-labeling-and-classification). |

### CP: Contingency Planning

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CP-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the contingency planning policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Contingency Plan will hold the procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [RC-4.1](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-41-contingency-plan-cp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| CP-2 | Contingency Plan | System-Specific | Planned | The Platform Team will write the Contingency Plan, with Fleet Operations writing the fleet and ground segment sections. It names the essential functions and their recovery objectives, and the roster with a backup for every role. It also sets the restoration order, the backup policy, the manual fallbacks, and the alternate site arrangements. The ISSM reviews it, and the Configuration Control Board approves it. A printed copy is kept at each site, so it can be read when the identity provider is down. The SSP describes it under [RC-4.1](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-41-contingency-plan-cp). |
| CP-2(1) | Contingency Plan \| Coordinate with Related Plans | System-Specific | Planned | The plan will be coordinated with the related plans and parties. These are the Incident Response Plan, the parent organization's continuity of operations and occupant emergency plans, the alternate site's operator, and the CSSP. The record of that coordination is kept with the plan. The SSP describes it under [RC-4.1](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-41-contingency-plan-cp). |
| CP-2(2) | Contingency Plan \| Capacity Planning | System-Specific | Planned | Capacity will be planned for a contingency. The alternate site holds warm standbys sized for Tier 1. Recovery spokes in US Gov Arizona are sized to take Tier 2 if the data center is lost. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-2(3) | Contingency Plan \| Resume Mission and Business Functions | System-Specific | Planned | Essential functions will be resumed within each tier's recovery time objective: 4 hours for Tier 1, 24 hours for Tier 2, and 7 days for Tier 3. The program manager approves those objectives from the business impact analysis. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.1](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-31-recovery-objective-definition-rtorpo). |
| CP-2(5) | Contingency Plan \| Continue Mission and Business Functions | System-Specific | Planned | Essential functions will continue through a disruption. The fleet keeps flying from the ground control stations with local smart card sign-in, and aircraft keep their recordings until the data lake returns. Analysts work from the last delivered products, and mission planning reverts to manual if the planning agent is unavailable. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.5](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-35-manualfail-safe-operational-fallback-readiness). |
| CP-2(8) | Contingency Plan \| Identify Critical Assets | System-Specific | Planned | The plan will name the critical assets behind each essential function, taken from the business impact analysis. Examples are the identity provider, the PKI and HSMs, the signing path, and the ground segment's configuration. The SSP describes it under [RC-4.1](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-41-contingency-plan-cp). |
| CP-3 | Contingency Training | System-Specific | Planned | Everyone with a contingency role will be trained when they take the role, after a system change, and each year. That includes the operators, the restore operators, and the Tier 0 administrators. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.5](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-35-manualfail-safe-operational-fallback-readiness). |
| CP-3(1) | Contingency Training \| Simulated Events | System-Specific | Planned | Training will include simulated events. Fleet drills on degraded operations start when the fleet integrates in Phase 3. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.5](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-35-manualfail-safe-operational-fallback-readiness). |
| CP-4 | Contingency Plan Testing | System-Specific | Planned | The plan will be tested. Each quarter the Platform Team restores a sample from every tier and measures the result against its objectives, and production traffic fails between the data center's two circuits. A failover exercise runs each year, and a tier that misses its objective is raised to the AO. The SSP describes them under [RC-3.2](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-32-backup-recovery-testing), [RC-3.3](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-33-disaster-recovery-capabilities). |
| CP-4(1) | Contingency Plan Testing \| Coordinate with Related Plans | System-Specific | Planned | The yearly failover exercise will be coordinated with the owners of related plans, including the Incident Response Plan's owner and the CSSP. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.3](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-33-disaster-recovery-capabilities). |
| CP-4(2) | Contingency Plan Testing \| Alternate Processing Site | System-Specific | Planned | The yearly failover exercise will run at the alternate site, proving its standbys, its circuit, and its readiness to take the workload. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.3](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-33-disaster-recovery-capabilities). |
| CP-6 | Alternate Storage Site | System-Specific | Planned | The alternate site will store a copy of every backup, and immutable Blob storage in US Gov Arizona will store a second copy. No single site or region holds every copy. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-6(1) | Alternate Storage Site \| Separation from Primary Site | System-Specific | Planned | The alternate site will be a parent organization facility in a different region from the data center, far enough away that no regional event reaches both. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-6(2) | Alternate Storage Site \| Recovery Time and Recovery Point Objectives | System-Specific | Planned | Backups will be replicated to the alternate storage sites often enough to meet each tier's recovery point objective. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-6(3) | Alternate Storage Site \| Accessibility | System-Specific | Planned | Events that could leave the alternate site unreachable will be planned for: a regional DISN outage, the parent organization's own emergency, or a travel restriction. In each case, Tier 2 restores into recovery spokes in US Gov Arizona, managed from the cloud. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-7 | Alternate Processing Site | System-Specific | Planned | The alternate site will serve as the alternate processing site, holding warm standbys for Tier 1, including domain controllers, an issuing certificate authority, and CyberArk. Tier 1 services run there within their 4-hour recovery time, and Tier 2 services restore into the recovery spokes in US Gov Arizona. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-7(1) | Alternate Processing Site \| Separation from Primary Site | System-Specific | Planned | The alternate processing site will be far enough from the data center that no regional event reaches both. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-7(2) | Alternate Processing Site \| Accessibility | System-Specific | Planned | The same accessibility plans that cover the alternate storage site will cover processing, with US Gov Arizona as the fallback when the alternate site cannot be reached. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-7(3) | Alternate Processing Site \| Priority of Service | System-Specific | Planned | The facility agreement will give KESTREL priority access to the alternate site in an area-wide emergency, and it names who may activate the site. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-7(4) | Alternate Processing Site \| Preparation for Use | System-Specific | Planned | The alternate site will be kept ready for use. Its standbys stay warm, a second HSM holds the escrowed keys, and a copy of every backup and two privileged access workstations are staged there. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-8 | Telecommunications Services | Hybrid | Planned | Each of the data center's two circuits will come from a different carrier, and the alternate site will have a third. All three ride DISN, whose transport KESTREL inherits. Production traffic fails between the data center's circuits each quarter. **Inherited from DISA:** DISN transport for the circuits, with priority restoration. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-8(1) | Telecommunications Services \| Priority of Service Provisions | System-Specific | Planned | Every carrier agreement will carry priority restoration of service. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-8(2) | Telecommunications Services \| Single Points of Failure | System-Specific | Planned | No single point of failure will be able to cut the data center off. Each circuit runs on its own path, through its own building entry, to a different meet-me point. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-8(3) | Telecommunications Services \| Separation of Primary and Alternate Providers | System-Specific | Planned | The data center's two circuits will come from different carriers, so the loss of one carrier does not take both. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-8(4) | Telecommunications Services \| Provider Contingency Plan | System-Specific | Planned | Every carrier agreement will require the carrier to keep a contingency plan of its own. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-34-alternate-site-and-telecommunications-readiness). |
| CP-9 | System Backup | System-Specific | Planned | Backups will follow three tiers set from the business impact analysis. Tier 1 is replicated continuously with a daily full backup, Tier 2 is backed up daily, and Tier 3 weekly. Azure Backup protects cloud services, and Veeam protects the data center. Services that cannot be backed up directly are exported on schedule, and fleet equipment is captured with the manufacturers' tools in maintenance windows. Every resource is bound to its tier's policy when it is created. The SSP describes them under [RC-1.1](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-11-backup-coverage-strategy), [RC-1.2](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-12-automated-backup-for-supported-services), [RC-1.3](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-13-backup-unsupported-services), [RC-1.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-14-otlegacy-configuration-and-engineering-backup), [RC-1.5](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-15-backup-policy-enforcement), [RC-1.7](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-17-backup-compliance-and-coverage-monitoring), [RC-2.3](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-23-backup-immutability-and-redundancy), [RC-3.1](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-31-recovery-objective-definition-rtorpo). |
| CP-9(1) | System Backup \| Testing for Reliability and Integrity | System-Specific | Planned | Backup jobs will be checked for reliability and integrity. Job results reach Splunk, a failure alerts the backup operators, and a sample is test-restored each week. The SSP describes it under [RC-1.6](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-16-backup-health-and-operations-monitoring). |
| CP-9(2) | System Backup \| Test Restoration Using Sampling | System-Specific | Planned | A sample from every tier will be restored each quarter, rotating so every Tier 1 system is restored at least once a year. The registry restore re-verifies every signature. The SSP describes it under [RC-3.2](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-32-backup-recovery-testing). |
| CP-9(3) | System Backup \| Separate Storage for Critical Information | System-Specific | Planned | Backups of critical information, such as the identity provider and the PKI, will be stored separately from the systems they protect. They sit in locked storage at the alternate site and in the second region. HSM key backups go only to the alternate site's HSM. The SSP describes it under [RC-2.3](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-23-backup-immutability-and-redundancy). |
| CP-9(5) | System Backup \| Transfer to Alternate Storage Site | System-Specific | Planned | Backup copies will be transferred to the alternate site and to the second IL5 region often enough to meet each tier's recovery point. The SSP describes it under [RC-2.3](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-23-backup-immutability-and-redundancy). |
| CP-9(8) | System Backup \| Cryptographic Protection | System-Specific | Planned | Each Veeam backup set will be encrypted under its own key rooted in the nShield HSMs, and Azure Backup vaults use customer-managed keys in Key Vault Premium. The SSP describes it under [RC-2.2](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-22-backup-data-encryption). |
| CP-10 | System Recovery and Reconstitution | System-Specific | Planned | Systems will be restored to a known state: their last backup from before the disruption, or before the compromise if an incident caused it. A restored system returns to service only after its image and configuration match their signed baselines, a compliance scan passes, and its logs reach Splunk. The restoration order is agreed in advance. The SSP describes it under [RC-4.1](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-41-contingency-plan-cp). |
| CP-10(2) | System Recovery and Reconstitution \| Transaction Recovery | System-Specific | Planned | Point-in-time restore will recover database transactions to within each tier's recovery point. The SSP describes it under [RC-1.2](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-12-automated-backup-for-supported-services). |
| CP-10(4) | System Recovery and Reconstitution \| Restore Within Time Period | System-Specific | Planned | Services will be restorable from a known-good image within set times. Every production spoke keeps the previous certified release ready to roll back to, and each model endpoint can return to its previous certified version in minutes. Rollback is rehearsed before each model is certified. The SSP describes them under [AP-4.6](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-46-application-rollback-progressive-delivery-and-feature-flag-governance), [AI-6.6](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-66-rollbackkill-switch-readiness-check), [AI-8.14](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-814-rollbackkill-switch-mechanism). |

### IA: Identification and Authentication

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IA-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the identification and authentication policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Account Management Plan (AMP) will hold the procedures that carry it out, covering authenticators, assurance levels, and sessions. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [ID-5.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-51-account-management-plan-amp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| IA-2 | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) | System-Specific | Planned | Every person will be uniquely identified and authenticated before reaching anything in KESTREL. Active Directory in the mission data center will hold each user's account, and Entra ID will authenticate cloud sign-in against a synchronized copy of it. Group or shared accounts will not be used for everyday access. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.3](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-13-centralized-identity-platform). |
| IA-2(1) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Multi-factor Authentication to Privileged Accounts | System-Specific | Planned | Privileged accounts will authenticate with a CAC, which combines the card with its PIN. Administrators will sign in with the card first, through Entra certificate-based authentication or Active Directory smart card logon. Only then does CyberArk or Entra Privileged Identity Management grant a privileged role. The directory and station break-glass accounts are the one exception. They use console-only passwords under a compensating control, held by two custodians and changed after every use. CCSD tailoring action 6 (compensating control) applies, pending the AO's approval. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-2(2) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Multi-factor Authentication to Non-privileged Accounts | System-Specific | Planned | Non-privileged accounts will authenticate with a smart card as well, in every location. DoD users and performers will use their CAC, vendors an ECA credential, and partners a certificate from their own nation's PKI. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-2(5) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Individual Authentication with Group Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Built-in administrative accounts on appliances, hypervisors, and the HSMs will be reachable only through CyberArk. An administrator must first authenticate to CyberArk as an individual with a CAC. CyberArk then injects the shared credential into a recorded session, so the administrator never sees it and every use is tied to a person. The SSP describes it under [ID-4.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-44-privileged-credential-vaulting-and-session-brokering). |
| IA-2(8) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Access to Accounts — Replay Resistant | System-Specific | Planned | Certificate-based authentication will be used for every network sign-in, and it resists replay because each logon proves possession of the card's private key against a fresh challenge. The break-glass passwords are the only authenticators that would not resist replay. They are limited to named local consoles and never cross a network. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-2(12) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Acceptance of PIV Credentials | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will accept DoD CACs as PIV credentials. Entra certificate-based authentication will accept them in the cloud, and Active Directory smart card logon on premises. Each card's certificate is validated against DoD PKI and checked for revocation. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-3 | Device Identification and Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Devices will be authenticated before they connect. In the data center and at the alternate site, Cisco ISE will require 802.1X with EAP-TLS on every wired port, using device certificates from the program PKI. The operating sites follow in Phase 3. Each aircraft and ground control station will authenticate on the datalinks with its own program PKI device identity. Equipment that cannot hold a certificate will be admitted by its registered hardware address, and only to its own zone. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-37-otlegacy-device-identity-controls), [NE-1.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-17-network-access-control-nac8021x). |
| IA-4 | Identifier Management | System-Specific | Planned | Each person's identifier will be assigned at enrollment and bound to their CAC record, or to their sponsor's record for partners and vendors. IT Operations will assign identifiers through Jira Service Management and Entra ID Governance. Each new account will be checked against existing ones, so no person holds two identities and no identifier is assigned to a second person. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment), [ID-1.8](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-18-account-lifecycle-and-identity-data-quality). |
| IA-4(4) | Identifier Management \| Identify User Status | System-Specific | Planned | Each identifier will show the user's status. CAC affiliation will mark contractors, and a nationality attribute will mark partners and other foreign nationals. Roles and access policies can then tell these populations apart. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-5 | Authenticator Management | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will manage every authenticator it uses through a defined lifecycle. DoD issues and revokes the CACs. The program PKI will issue, renew, and revoke device and workload certificates, with its keys in the nShield HSMs and its certificates tracked in Keyfactor Command. Windows LAPS and group Managed Service Accounts will rotate local administrator and service passwords. Vendor-default credentials will be replaced before any server controller or fleet device is fielded. After a confirmed compromise, every affected authenticator will be reset. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-15-directory-and-tier-0-infrastructure-hardening), [ID-2.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-22-credential-management), [ID-3.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-37-otlegacy-device-identity-controls), [DI-3.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-32-secure-compute-baselines), [RS-3.4](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-34-eradication-and-threat-removal). |
| IA-5(1) | Authenticator Management \| Password-based Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Passwords will remain only on the break-glass accounts. Each password will be split between two custodians, sealed, and changed after every use. The AMP will set its length and composition. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-5(2) | Authenticator Management \| Public Key-based Authentication | Hybrid | Planned | Certificate validation will build a path to an approved trust anchor and check revocation at each session. DoD PKI, the External Certificate Authorities, and approved partner PKIs supply the anchors. Services will accept a cached revocation response for up to 24 hours, and the ground control stations will check a local list refreshed daily and before each flight. Private keys stay on the CAC or in the HSMs, and service accounts will authenticate with certificates wherever they can. **Inherited from DoD PKI:** The DoD and External Certificate Authority trust anchors. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship), [ID-2.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-22-credential-management), [ID-3.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-32-application-and-service-account-identities). |
| IA-5(6) | Authenticator Management \| Protection of Authenticators | System-Specific | Planned | Authenticators will be kept out of code, images, and settings. Each cloud spoke's Key Vault will hold that spoke's secrets, and CyberArk will vault administrative credentials and inject them only into recorded sessions. Pipeline and training jobs will receive short-lived tokens through workload identity rather than stored credentials. The foundation model is reached by workload identity with key-based access disabled, so no API key exists to protect. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-36-secrets-and-credentials-protection), [ID-4.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-44-privileged-credential-vaulting-and-session-brokering), [AP-2.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-21-ide-security-tools), [AP-2.25](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-225-ci-credential-and-secrets-management), [AI-4.19](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-419-training-credential-secrets-management), [AI-8.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-83-third-partyfoundation-model-api-dependency-governance). |
| IA-6 | Authentication Feedback | System-Specific | Planned | Sign-in pages and consoles will hide what a user types and will not say which part of a failed logon was wrong.
