Failed attempts will be limited as the AMP sets. A ground control station whose aircraft is airborne will delay the next prompt and alert instead of locking the account. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-7 | Cryptographic Module Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Operators of the nShield HSMs will authenticate with smart cards from the HSMs' own card sets, and sensitive key operations will need a quorum of those cards. Software cryptographic modules will authenticate their callers through the identity platform. The SSP describes it under [DA-3.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-34-hsm-and-hardware-root-of-trust-management). |
| IA-8 | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) | System-Specific | Planned | People outside the organization will be identified and authenticated before reaching their part of KESTREL. Vendor support engineers will sign in with ECA Medium Hardware credentials through Entra certificate-based authentication. Partner systems will authenticate to the partner API with mutual TLS, using certificates from their own nation's PKI or an ECA. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-8(1) | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) \| Acceptance of PIV Credentials from Other Agencies | System-Specific | Planned | PIV credentials issued by other federal agencies will be accepted through the same certificate-based authentication, provided their issuers are on KESTREL's trust list. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-8(2) | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) \| Acceptance of External Authenticators | System-Specific | Planned | Only external authenticators from issuers on KESTREL's trust list will be accepted. The list names the External Certificate Authorities and each partner nation's issuing authorities, and adding a partner nation requires a CCSD revision. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-8(4) | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) \| Use of Defined Profiles | System-Specific | Planned | Partner connections will follow defined profiles. Partner systems will use X.509 certificates over mutual TLS. Partner identity providers, when they join in Phase 3, will federate using SAML or OIDC profiles agreed with each partner. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-11 | Re-authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Users will be asked to authenticate again when risk or context changes. Administrative consoles will always require fresh authentication, and activating a privileged role will too. Cloud and VDI sessions will end and require sign-in again when the AMP's session limits are reached, or sooner if continuous access evaluation finds the risk severe. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-26-continuous-authentication). |
| IA-12 | Identity Proofing | System-Specific | Planned | Every person will be proofed before KESTREL issues an account, at the assurance level the AMP sets for their population. DoD users and performers are proofed through their CAC issuance, and KESTREL binds each account to that record. Partners and vendors will be proofed through a KESTREL sponsor's attestation. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-12(2) | Identity Proofing \| Identity Evidence | System-Specific | Planned | The evidence behind each enrollment will be recorded in Jira Service Management. For DoD users and performers, that is the CAC record. For partners and vendors, it is the sponsor's attestation and the documents it relies on. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-12(3) | Identity Proofing \| Identity Evidence Validation and Verification | System-Specific | Planned | IT Operations will validate the evidence at enrollment. Each CAC will be checked against DoD PKI, and each sponsor's attestation against that sponsor's agreement with KESTREL. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-12(4) | Identity Proofing \| In-person Validation and Verification | Inherited | Inherited | DoD validates each person's identity evidence in person when it issues their CAC. KESTREL relies on that step and does not repeat it. |
| IA-12(5) | Identity Proofing \| Address Confirmation | System-Specific | Planned | For DoD users and performers, CAC issuance confirms the address of record. For partners and vendors, a registration code or notice of proofing will be sent out of band to the address their sponsor records. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |

### IR: Incident Response

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IR-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the incident response policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Incident Response Plan will hold the procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [RS-4.1](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-41-incident-response-plan-irp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| IR-2 | Incident Response Training | System-Specific | Planned | Everyone with an incident response role will be trained on KESTREL's runbooks when they take the role and each year after. That covers the Security Team, the Platform Team, IT Operations, the Data Team, and Fleet Operations. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.2](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-12-incident-response-team-structure-and-training). |
| IR-2(1) | Incident Response Training \| Simulated Events | System-Specific | Planned | Training will include simulated incidents, so responders practice the runbooks rather than only reading them. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.2](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-12-incident-response-team-structure-and-training). |
| IR-2(2) | Incident Response Training \| Automated Training Environments | System-Specific | Planned | Training will run in the exercise environment, which mirrors production's tools without touching production. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.2](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-12-incident-response-team-structure-and-training). |
| IR-2(3) | Incident Response Training \| Breach | Inherited | Inherited | Training on responding to a breach of personal information will come from the DoD component privacy program, which KESTREL inherits. |
| IR-3 | Incident Response Testing | System-Specific | Planned | The IRP will be tested twice a year by tabletop exercise, one with an aircraft or ground segment scenario and one with an AI scenario. From Phase 3, a functional exercise each year uses the real tools with the CSSP. Each exercise's findings are tracked, and the IRP is updated from them. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.3](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-13-incident-response-plan-testing-and-exercises). |
| IR-3(2) | Incident Response Testing \| Coordination with Related Plans | System-Specific | Planned | Exercises will be coordinated with the owners of related plans. The yearly functional exercise includes the Contingency Plan's owners and the CSSP, and it rehearses the handoff from incident response to recovery. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.3](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-13-incident-response-plan-testing-and-exercises). |
| IR-4 | Incident Handling | Hybrid | Planned | Incidents will be handled through preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery, as the IRP sets out. The ISSM leads each one in Jira Service Management, and owning teams act on their own systems at the ISSM's direction. The CSSP triages around the clock and contains what cannot wait through pre-approved playbooks. Fleet containment is manual, and nothing acts on an aircraft in flight. **Inherited from the CSSP:** Around-the-clock triage and pre-approved containment. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.5](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-55-endpoint-response), [RS-1.1](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-11-incident-response-development), [RS-2.2](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-22-incident-scoped-log-analysis-and-investigation), [RS-2.5](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-25-automated-severity-scoring-and-escalation), [RS-3.2](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-32-automated-containment-and-isolation-procedures), [RS-3.4](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-34-eradication-and-threat-removal), [RS-3.6](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-36-recovery-and-return-to-operations-validation), [RS-3.7](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-37-systemic-lessons-learned-process). |
| IR-4(1) | Incident Handling \| Automated Incident Handling Processes | System-Specific | Planned | Incident handling will be automated where it is safe. Splunk SOAR enriches incidents, opens and updates their records, and runs containment playbooks that can take only listed actions. Accounts are disabled and sessions revoked automatically, and non-production hosts are isolated automatically. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.5](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-55-endpoint-response), [RS-3.1](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-31-soar-capabilities). |
| IR-4(4) | Incident Handling \| Information Correlation | System-Specific | Planned | Information from every incident will be correlated in Splunk Enterprise Security and Defender XDR, so related events across hosts, identities, and the network are seen as one incident. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.5](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-55-endpoint-response). |
| IR-4(11) | Incident Handling \| Integrated Incident Response Team | System-Specific | Planned | One integrated incident response team will handle every incident. The ISSM leads it, with the Security Team, the CSSP, and the owning teams' responders working from the same runbooks and the same record. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.2](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-12-incident-response-team-structure-and-training). |
| IR-5 | Incident Monitoring | System-Specific | Planned | Every incident will be tracked in its Jira Service Management record, from declaration to closure, with its actions, findings, and evidence. The SSP describes it under [RS-2.1](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-21-automated-incident-creation-and-enrichment). |
| IR-5(1) | Incident Monitoring \| Automated Tracking, Data Collection, and Analysis | System-Specific | Planned | Correlated alerts above the declaration threshold will open an incident record automatically. Each record collects the affected asset's owner, team, criticality, and recent changes as the incident proceeds. The SSP describes it under [RS-2.1](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-21-automated-incident-creation-and-enrichment). |
| IR-6 | Incident Reporting | Hybrid | Planned | Incidents will be reported on the IRP's time limits. The ISSM notifies the AO, and the CSSP reports up the DoD reporting chain under CJCSM 6510.01B. The foreign disclosure officer notifies partner nations, the privacy officer reports breaches of personal information, and the performer reports incidents on its own laptops to DC3. **Inherited from the CSSP:** Reporting to the DoD reporting chain under CJCSM 6510.01B. The SSP describes them under [RS-1.5](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-15-automated-notification-workflows), [RS-1.6](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-16-incident-reporting-and-external-communications). |
| IR-6(1) | Incident Reporting \| Automated Reporting | System-Specific | Planned | A declared incident will notify the CSSP's operations center and page the on-call analyst automatically. If the service desk or the circuits are down, Splunk pages directly, sending only an incident ID and severity. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.5](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-15-automated-notification-workflows). |
| IR-6(3) | Incident Reporting \| Supply Chain Coordination | System-Specific | Planned | Incidents that involve a supplier's product will be coordinated with that supplier, under the notification terms in its contract. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.6](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-16-incident-reporting-and-external-communications). |
| IR-7 | Incident Response Assistance | System-Specific | Planned | The CSSP will provide incident response support around the clock under its service agreement, including triage and pre-approved containment. The ISSM tracks each CSSP directive to completion. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.7](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-17-cyber-defense-service-provider-alignment). |
| IR-7(1) | Incident Response Assistance \| Automation Support for Availability of Information and Support | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk will forward all telemetry to the CSSP automatically, so its analysts have the same information as the Security Team, and a stalled feed raises an alert. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.7](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-17-cyber-defense-service-provider-alignment). |
| IR-8 | Incident Response Plan | System-Specific | Planned | The ISSM will have an interim IRP approved in Phase 1 for the interim authorization to test, covering declaration, reporting to the CSSP, and who acts. The full IRP, with its runbooks, follows in Phase 2. It is revised each year and after each exercise. The SSP describes it under [RS-4.1](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-41-incident-response-plan-irp). |
| IR-8(1) | Incident Response Plan \| Breaches | System-Specific | Planned | The IRP will cover breaches of personal information, including the privacy officer's reporting duty and the notice owed to the people affected. The SSP describes it under [RS-4.1](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-41-incident-response-plan-irp). |

### MA: Maintenance

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MA-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the maintenance policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Configuration Management Plan's maintenance section, written by IT Operations, will hold the procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| MA-2 | Controlled Maintenance | Hybrid | Planned | On-premises hardware maintenance will be scheduled in Jira Service Management, escorted, and recorded. The owning team's lead approves it, and Tier 0 maintenance also needs the Platform Team lead. Failed drives stay on site for sanitization. From Phase 3, fleet maintenance runs only in each operating site's weekly window, never while an aircraft under its stations is airborne. After maintenance, a compliance scan confirms the component still meets its baseline. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Maintenance of the cloud hardware. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-45-otlegacy-scheduled-maintenance-window-access), [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-2(2) | Controlled Maintenance \| Automated Maintenance Activities | System-Specific | Planned | Maintenance will be scheduled, tracked, and recorded in Jira Service Management, so each maintenance action and its change share one record. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-3 | Maintenance Tools | System-Specific | Planned | The Security Team will approve the diagnostic tools that maintenance may use. Each tool is scanned at the media intake station before use. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-3(1) | Maintenance Tools \| Inspect Tools | System-Specific | Planned | Maintenance tools will be inspected before use, both those KESTREL holds and those a vendor brings, to confirm they are approved and unmodified. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-45-otlegacy-scheduled-maintenance-window-access), [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-3(2) | Maintenance Tools \| Inspect Media | System-Specific | Planned | Media carrying diagnostic or test programs will be scanned for malicious code at the media intake station before it is used on any KESTREL system. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-45-otlegacy-scheduled-maintenance-window-access), [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-3(3) | Maintenance Tools \| Prevent Unauthorized Removal | System-Specific | Planned | Maintenance equipment will not leave with KESTREL information on it. Failed drives stay on site, and any other component leaving the facility first has its storage sanitized with Blancco, or removed and kept. HSMs are zeroized before they ship. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-4 | Nonlocal Maintenance | Hybrid | Planned | Vendor engineers will perform remote maintenance only from the dedicated vendor host pool in Azure Virtual Desktop. They sign in with ECA Medium Hardware credentials, and only for an open Jira Service Management case. CyberArk brokers and records each session, which lasts at most eight hours and ends when the case closes. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Nonlocal maintenance of the cloud hardware. The SSP describes it under [ID-4.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-47-access-process-for-third-party-support). |
| MA-4(3) | Nonlocal Maintenance \| Comparable Security and Sanitization | System-Specific | Planned | Remote maintenance will run from systems KESTREL controls. Vendor sessions start in the vendor host pool, which is built to KESTREL's own VDI baseline, rather than from the vendor's device. The SSP describes it under [ID-4.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-47-access-process-for-third-party-support). |
| MA-5 | Maintenance Personnel | Hybrid | Planned | Only authorized people will perform maintenance. KESTREL's own staff do most of it. A vendor engineer working on site is escorted at all times, and one working remotely is limited to the brokered session for their case. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Maintenance personnel for the cloud hardware. The SSP describes it under [ID-4.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-45-otlegacy-scheduled-maintenance-window-access). |
| MA-5(1) | Maintenance Personnel \| Individuals Without Appropriate Access | System-Specific | Planned | Vendor engineers without KESTREL access will be escorted on site at all times by an authorized KESTREL staff member. They work only on the equipment in their case. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-6 | Timely Maintenance | Hybrid | Planned | Support agreements will set replacement times for the HSMs, identity servers, and hub firewalls. Spares cover the mission's tolerance for downtime, including spare stations and aircraft for the fleet. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Timely maintenance of the cloud hardware. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |

### MP: Media Protection

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MP-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the media protection policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The media protection procedures, which Fleet Operations and IT Operations write, will carry it out. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| MP-2 | Media Access | System-Specific | Planned | Removable media will be prohibited except for three classes: each aircraft's mission storage modules, encrypted government media carrying prior collection, and the datalink key loaders. Mission storage modules can be read only at a ground control station and the IT/OT DMZ, and key loaders are held under two-person custody. Across the IT estate, removable storage is blocked by policy. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |
| MP-3 | Media Marking | System-Specific | Planned | Mission storage modules will be marked CUI, and so will every other piece of removable media KESTREL holds. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |
| MP-4 | Media Storage | System-Specific | Planned | Mission storage modules will be kept in each station's locked store when they are not in an aircraft. Key loaders are stored under two-person custody. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |
| MP-5 | Media Transport | System-Specific | Planned | Mission storage modules will be encrypted under keys in the aircraft's crypto module, logged when they leave an aircraft, and carried by a named custodian in controlled containers. Encrypted government media is carried to the media intake station. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |
| MP-6 | Media Sanitization | Hybrid | Planned | Media will be sanitized before it leaves KESTREL's control. Failed drives and retired storage modules are purged on site with Blancco to NIST SP 800-88 and verified. Retired or repaired HSMs and datalink crypto modules are zeroized. Cloud storage media is sanitized by the provider under its authorization. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Sanitization of cloud storage media. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-23-resource-decommissioning-governance), [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |
| MP-6(1) | Media Sanitization \| Review, Approve, Track, Document, and Verify | System-Specific | Planned | Each sanitization will be reviewed, approved, tracked, documented, and verified. The decommissioning record in Jira Service Management holds the method, the result, and a certificate of destruction for each item. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-23-resource-decommissioning-governance), [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |
| MP-6(2) | Media Sanitization \| Equipment Testing | System-Specific | Planned | Sanitization equipment and procedures will be tested so they keep achieving the intended result. Blancco verifies each wipe as it completes, and the equipment is checked on a schedule. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |
| MP-6(3) | Media Sanitization \| Nondestructive Techniques | Not applicable | Not applicable | Portable storage never connects to KESTREL. Government media is read at the standalone intake station, where wiping it would destroy the collection it carries. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |
| MP-7 | Media Use | System-Specific | Planned | Removable storage will be blocked on every workstation, desktop, and server by device control policy. The one exception is the media intake station, which reads only encrypted government media. Mission storage modules are used only in aircraft and ground control stations. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control), [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |

### PL: Planning

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PL-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the planning policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The SSP and the governing plans hold the procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve the policy and plans, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework), [GV-5.3](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-53-system-security-plan-ssp). |
| PL-2 | System Security and Privacy Plans | System-Specific | Planned | The ISSM will keep KESTREL's System Security Plan in OSCAL from its first version and publish it to eMASS. It describes the boundary, the components, the information types and categorization, and how each SADD outcome is implemented. The AO approves an initial SSP before the interim authorization to test, and the full SSP with the authorization package. It is reviewed each year and with each continuous monitoring cycle. The SSP describes it under [GV-5.3](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-53-system-security-plan-ssp). |
| PL-4 | Rules of Behavior | System-Specific | Planned | Every user will sign the rules of behavior before their account is created, and each year after. A lapsed acknowledgment disables the account, and the ISSM refers violations to the PSO. The SSP describes it under [GV-2.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-24-rules-of-behavior-and-acceptable-use-policy). |
| PL-4(1) | Rules of Behavior \| Social Media and External Site/Application Usage Restrictions | System-Specific | Planned | The rules of behavior will restrict what users may post about KESTREL on social media and external sites, and what external applications they may use with KESTREL information. The SSP describes it under [GV-2.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-24-rules-of-behavior-and-acceptable-use-policy). |
| PL-8 | Security and Privacy Architectures | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL's security architecture will be the SADD, built from the CCSD and the SABER. The AO approves it as the design basis, and it is rebuilt whenever the CCSD, the system description, or the SABER version changes. The SSP describes it under [GV-5.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-51-security-architecture-and-design-document-sadd). |
| PL-9 | Central Management | System-Specific | Planned | Security controls that apply everywhere will be managed centrally. Policy as code is defined once, in GitLab, and deployed to every location by the pipeline. The SSP describes it under [AP-2.19](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-219-policy-as-code-evaluation). |
| PL-10 | Baseline Selection | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL's baseline will be selected from the CNSSI 1253 columns for its categorization of High confidentiality, High integrity, and Moderate availability. The SSP describes it under [GV-5.5](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-55-security-categorization). |
| PL-11 | Baseline Tailoring | System-Specific | Planned | The baseline will be tailored in the CCSD, through tailoring actions the PMO ISSE drafts, the SCA reviews, and the AO approves. Each action records its rationale and the AO's decision. The SSP describes it under [GV-5.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-54-categorization-and-control-selection-document-ccsd). |

### PM: Program Management

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PM-3 | Information Security and Privacy Resources | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from the parent organization:** Security and privacy resourcing at the enterprise level. |
| PM-4 | Plan of Action and Milestones Process | System-Specific | Planned | One POA&M process will cover every finding. Items live in eMASS from Phase 1, and milestones are reviewed each month and reported to the AO each quarter. An ISSO closes an item only after verifying the fix. From Phase 2, one ranking in Jira orders remediation across every team by risk. The SSP describes them under [RK-1.8](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-18-plan-of-action-and-milestones-poam), [RK-3.1](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-31-risk-based-remediation-prioritization). |
| PM-5(1) | System Inventory \| Inventory of Personally Identifiable Information | System-Specific | Planned | The privacy officer will keep an inventory of the personal information KESTREL holds and where each kind is stored. That is user and service desk records, and incidental imagery of people. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-41-privacy-program-management). |
| PM-6 | Measures of Performance | System-Specific | Planned | Security performance will be measured and reported. The steering committee reviews a security posture dashboard in Splunk each month, and the AI/ML Governance Review Board sends a posture report to it each quarter. The risk register and the evidence repository feed both. The SSP describes them under [GV-1.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-14-security-governance-and-steering-committee), [GV-4.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-44-aiml-governance-review-board), [RK-1.3](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-13-risk-register-and-tracking), [CO-1.3](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-13-compliance-evidence-collection-and-retention). |
| PM-7 | Enterprise Architecture | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL's security architecture will be the SADD, which the AO approves as the design basis, and its components and data flows are described in the System Description. The SSP describes it under [GV-5.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-51-security-architecture-and-design-document-sadd). |
| PM-8 | Critical Infrastructure Plan | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from DoD enterprise services:** Critical infrastructure planning at the department level. |
| PM-9 | Risk Management Strategy | System-Specific | Planned | The risk management strategy will be the Risk Management Program Charter. It sets one assessment method based on NIST SP 800-30, the program's risk appetite, and the chain of authority for accepting risk. The AO approves the appetite statement, and the charter is reviewed each year. The SSP describes them under [RK-1.1](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-11-risk-assessment-methodology), [RK-1.2](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-12-risk-appetite-and-tolerance-definition). |
| PM-10 | Authorization Process | System-Specific | Planned | The authorization process will run from the interim authorization to test in Phase 1 to the ATO decision on 2028-09-30, managed by the ISSM in eMASS. After that, ongoing authorization keeps it current, with agreed reauthorization triggers and a status report to the AO each quarter. The SSP describes it under [GV-5.7](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-57-authorization-to-operate-ato-process). |
| PM-11 | Mission and Business Process Definition | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL's mission processes will be defined in the business impact analysis, from flying the aircraft to collecting, analyzing, releasing, and retraining, with how long each can be lost. Each AI use case is defined in the inventory and approved by the review board before work starts. The SSP describes them under [GV-4.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-41-aiml-use-case-inventory), [GV-4.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-44-aiml-governance-review-board), [RK-3.2](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-32-business-impact-analysis-bia). |
| PM-13 | Security and Privacy Workforce | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from DoD enterprise services:** The DoD cyber workforce program under DoDM 8140.03. |
| PM-14 | Testing, Training, and Monitoring | System-Specific | Planned | Testing, training, and monitoring will be coordinated across the program. The parent organization's internal review office audits each governing plan at least once every two years, checking that its procedures are actually carried out. The SSP describes it under [CO-3.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-31-internal-audit-program). |
| PM-17 | Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information on External Systems | System-Specific | Planned | Contractors and other parties that hold KESTREL's CUI on their own systems will meet DFARS 252.204-7012 and NIST SP 800-171, under their contracts. Before any CUI is shared, the supply chain lead confirms the supplier's SPRS score and its CMMC Level 2 status. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| PM-18 | Privacy Program Plan | System-Specific | Planned | The privacy officer will maintain the Privacy Program Charter and Policy, which sets KESTREL's privacy program at the Privacy Overlay's Low tier within the DoD component privacy program. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-41-privacy-program-management). |
| PM-19 | Privacy Program Leadership Role | System-Specific | Planned | The privacy officer will lead KESTREL's privacy program, approving the handling of personal information and each new training set. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-41-privacy-program-management). |
| PM-20 | Dissemination of Privacy Program Information | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from the DoD component privacy office:** Privacy program information published by the component. |
| PM-20(1) | Dissemination of Privacy Program Information \| Privacy Policies on Websites, Applications, and Digital Services | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from the DoD component privacy office:** Privacy policies on the component websites. |
| PM-21 | Accounting of Disclosures | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from the DoD component privacy office:** Accounting of disclosures under the component privacy program. |
| PM-22 | Personally Identifiable Information Quality Management | System-Specific | Planned | The quality of personal information will be managed under the privacy program. Users correct the attributes KESTREL holds about them through Jira Service Management, and CAC and partner attributes are corrected at their source. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-41-privacy-program-management). |
| PM-24 | Data Integrity Board | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from the DoD component privacy office:** The component Data Integrity Board. |
| PM-25 | Minimization of Personally Identifiable Information Used in Testing, Training, and Research | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from the DoD component privacy office:** Component policy minimizing PII in testing, training, and research. |
| PM-26 | Complaint Management | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from the DoD component privacy office:** Complaint management under the component privacy program. |
| PM-27 | Privacy Reporting | Inherited | Inherited | **Inherited from the DoD component privacy office:** Privacy reporting by the component. |
| PM-28 | Risk Framing | System-Specific | Planned | The program's risk framing will be set in the risk appetite statement. Appetite is lowest where a failure could reach an aircraft or a key, and moderate for analytic availability and development. The program manager drafts the statement and the AO approves it. The SSP describes it under [RK-1.2](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-12-risk-appetite-and-tolerance-definition). |

The SSP describes it under [CO-2.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-21-continuous-monitoring-plan-conmon). |
