The SSP describes them under [AI-1.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-12-privacy-requirements-definition), [CO-4.2](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-42-privacy-impact-assessments-pia). |
| PT-3 | Personally Identifiable Information Processing Purposes | System-Specific | Planned | Personal information will be processed only for stated purposes. User and service desk records support account management and support, and incidental imagery of people is kept only where a detection task needs it. No model is trained to identify individuals. The SSP describes them under [AI-1.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-12-privacy-requirements-definition), [CO-4.2](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-42-privacy-impact-assessments-pia). |
| PT-4 | Consent | Inherited | Inherited | Consent will be handled under the DoD component privacy program, which KESTREL inherits. |
| PT-5 | Privacy Notice | System-Specific | Planned | The account request form will carry a Privacy Act statement, so each user receives notice when their personal information is collected. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.2](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-42-privacy-impact-assessments-pia). |
| PT-5(2) | Privacy Notice \| Privacy Act Statements | System-Specific | Planned | A Privacy Act statement will be given wherever KESTREL collects personal information directly from a person, starting with the account request form. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.2](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-42-privacy-impact-assessments-pia). |
| PT-6 | System of Records Notice | Inherited | Inherited | User and service desk records will be covered by the DoD-wide system of records notices that the component privacy office names, which KESTREL inherits. |
| PT-6(1) | System of Records Notice \| Routine Uses | Inherited | Inherited | The routine uses of those records will be reviewed under the DoD-wide notices, which KESTREL inherits. |
| PT-6(2) | System of Records Notice \| Exemption Rules | Inherited | Inherited | Exemption rules for those records will come from the DoD-wide notices, which KESTREL inherits. |
| PT-7 | Specific Categories of Personally Identifiable Information | System-Specific | Planned | The Privacy Impact Assessment will identify any special category of personal information KESTREL processes. KESTREL collects no Social Security numbers, and accounts key on the CAC DoD ID number. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.2](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-42-privacy-impact-assessments-pia). |
| PT-7(1) | Specific Categories of Personally Identifiable Information \| Social Security Numbers | Not applicable | Not applicable | KESTREL collects no Social Security numbers. Accounts key on the CAC DoD ID number. |
| PT-7(2) | Specific Categories of Personally Identifiable Information \| First Amendment Information | System-Specific | Planned | Intelligence oversight rules bar KESTREL from collecting information about how anyone exercises their First Amendment rights. The compliance mapping register records that obligation. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-41-privacy-program-management). |
| PT-8 | Computer Matching Requirements | Not applicable | Not applicable | KESTREL runs no computer matching program. |

### RA: Risk Assessment

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RA-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the risk assessment policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Risk Management Program Charter and the Vulnerability and Patch Management Plan will hold the procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve them, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DI-7.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-71-vulnerability-and-patch-management-plan-vpmp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| RA-2 | Security Categorization | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will be categorized High for confidentiality and integrity, and Moderate for availability, by CNSSI 1253's high-water mark over the CCSD's 18 information types. The AO concurred in the categorization on 2026-08-28, and it is reassessed with every CCSD revision. The SSP describes them under [GV-5.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-54-categorization-and-control-selection-document-ccsd), [GV-5.5](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-55-security-categorization). |
| RA-3 | Risk Assessment | System-Specific | Planned | Risk will be assessed with one method, based on NIST SP 800-30, and recorded in one register. Risks come from threat models, release and model certification scores, the AI threat assessment, and the SCA's assessment. The SCA's Risk Assessment Report goes to the AO before the ATO decision, and the register is reviewed each month. The SSP describes them under [AP-4.5](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-45-deployment-risk-threshold-evaluation), [AI-6.5](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-65-model-deployment-risk-threshold-evaluation), [GV-4.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-41-aiml-use-case-inventory), [GV-4.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-42-program-level-ai-threat-assessment), [RK-1.3](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-13-risk-register-and-tracking), [RK-1.7](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-17-risk-assessment-report-rar). |
| RA-3(1) | Risk Assessment \| Supply Chain Risk Assessment | System-Specific | Planned | Supply chain risk will be assessed each year for every Tier 1 supplier and the components KESTREL depends on most, including the foundation model's publisher. Single points of supply and countries of origin are recorded, and model choices record the supplier risks accepted. The SSP describes them under [AI-1.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-13-model-selection-and-justification), [GV-3.3](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-33-supply-chain-risk-assessment-and-dependency-mapping). |
| RA-5 | Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | System-Specific | Planned | Every host will be scanned for vulnerabilities by ACAS in every location, on a continuously updated feed. Containers are scanned before they are pushed and rescanned in the registry. Dependencies are reviewed at every merge request and matched daily against new disclosures after release. Applications get DAST in stage, and models are re-tested against new attacks each quarter. Findings are fixed on the VPMP's deadlines. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.8](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-48-vulnerability-and-patch-management), [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection), [AP-2.5](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-25-container-scanning), [AP-2.8](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-28-dependency-review), [AP-3.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-32-dast), [AP-5.12](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-512-fielded-dependency-vulnerability-monitoring), [AI-4.6](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-46-ai-dependency-vulnerability-scanning), [AI-7.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-71-automated-retraining-pipeline-security-assessments-and-patching), [AI-9.9](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-99-operational-adversarial-re-testing). |
| RA-5(2) | Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning \| Update Vulnerabilities to Be Scanned | System-Specific | Planned | ACAS's vulnerability feed will update continuously, and Dependency-Track and Xray pull new vulnerability data as it is published. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection). |
| RA-5(4) | Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning \| Discoverable Information | System-Specific | Planned | Tenable Attack Surface Management will watch KESTREL's public names and services from outside, and GitGuardian will watch public sources for KESTREL's code and credentials. The Security Team reviews the findings each month. The SSP describes it under [NE-3.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-37-external-attack-surface-management). |
| RA-5(5) | Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning \| Privileged Access | System-Specific | Planned | Vulnerability scans will run authenticated. Scan credentials for Tier 0 are vaulted in CyberArk and used only from a Tier 0 scanner. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection). |
| RA-5(11) | Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning \| Public Disclosure Program | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL's internet-reachable endpoints will be enrolled in the DoD Vulnerability Disclosure Program, which DC3 runs. The Security Team triages each relayed report and tracks it to closure like a penetration test finding. The SSP describes it under [AP-5.10](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-510-vulnerability-disclosure-program). |
| RA-7 | Risk Response | System-Specific | Planned | Each risk will get a recorded response: fix it, compensate for it, or accept it under the risk acceptance process. Release and model scores route anything outside their thresholds to the PMO ISSE. Anything above Very Low in the flight safety and key material rows goes to the AO. Assets that cannot be patched get a fixed set of compensating controls. Accepted design risks are tracked in their own register. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.8](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-48-vulnerability-and-patch-management), [DI-4.9](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-49-unpatchablelegacy-asset-compensating-controls), [AP-4.5](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-45-deployment-risk-threshold-evaluation), [AP-5.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-51-architecture-risk-tracking), [AI-6.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-64-risk-acceptance-and-approval-log), [AI-6.5](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-65-model-deployment-risk-threshold-evaluation), [GV-4.6](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-46-aiml-vendormodel-risk-assessment), [RK-1.4](../06-ssp/12-risk.md#rk-14-risk-acceptance-process). |
| RA-8 | Privacy Impact Assessments | System-Specific | Planned | The Privacy Impact Assessment, on DD Form 2930, will be approved in Phase 1, before user and service desk records and the prior collection imagery arrive. A new collection, sensor, AI use case, or partner release triggers a reassessment. The SSP describes them under [AI-1.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-12-privacy-requirements-definition), [CO-4.2](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-42-privacy-impact-assessments-pia). |
| RA-9 | Criticality Analysis | System-Specific | Planned | A criticality analysis will identify the components the mission depends on most. Each asset's criticality comes from the business impact analysis and its inventory tags. The command link, the stations, the identity provider, the HSMs and PKI, and the signing and registry path rank highest. Each model's robustness requirements reflect how much the mission relies on its output. The SSP describes them under [AI-1.6](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-16-robustness-requirements-definition), [AI-5.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-53-adversarial-evasion-robustness-testing), [RS-2.4](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-24-asset-criticality-and-business-impact-assessment). |

### SA: System and Services Acquisition

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SA-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the acquisition policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Supply Chain Risk Management Plan will hold the acquisition procedures, including the contract security requirements. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework), [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-2 | Allocation of Resources | System-Specific | Planned | Security will be planned and funded as part of each capability. The PMO ISSE turns the CCSD's controls into requirements that enter each team's backlog. The program managers hold a dedicated application security budget line, which funds closing the gaps the PMO ISSE finds. The SSP describes them under [AP-1.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-11-capability-gap-identification-and-planning), [AP-1.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-13-security-requirements-definition). |
| SA-3 | System Development Life Cycle | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will manage development through one lifecycle with security built into each stage. Every application, AI use case, and COTS product enters through intake, is threat-modeled before it is built, and is tested and certified before it is fielded. Roles for each stage are set in the ASP and the AISP. The SSP describes them under [AP-1.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-11-capability-gap-identification-and-planning), [AP-1.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-12-application-intake-and-onboarding), [AI-1.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-11-ai-use-case-intake-and-onboarding). |
| SA-4 | Acquisition Process | System-Specific | Planned | Each acquisition will state the security functions the product must provide, the evidence the supplier must deliver, and the supplier's configuration and supply chain duties. The PMO ISSE writes these requirements from the SADD, and the supply chain lead draws the contract terms from the clause library the SCRM plan sets out. Model selection records the security criteria each model and publisher was assessed against. The SSP describes them under [AP-1.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-13-security-requirements-definition), [AI-1.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-13-model-selection-and-justification), [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(1) | Acquisition Process \| Functional Properties of Controls | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to describe the functional properties of the security controls their products provide, as a clause in the Supply Chain Risk Management Plan's clause library. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(2) | Acquisition Process \| Design and Implementation Information for Controls | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to provide design and implementation information for the security controls in their products, as a clause in the clause library. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(5) | Acquisition Process \| System, Component, and Service Configurations | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to deliver their products in a secure configuration, with that configuration documented, as a clause in the clause library. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(9) | Acquisition Process \| Functions, Ports, Protocols, and Services in Use | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and services their products use. That information feeds KESTREL's PPSM registration and the CMP's list of permitted services. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(10) | Acquisition Process \| Use of Approved PIV Products | System-Specific | Planned | Products that handle PIV credentials, such as CAC readers and the identity platform, will be bought only from the products approved for FIPS 201 use. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-5 | System Documentation | System-Specific | Planned | Documentation for each certified model will be generated from its validation results. The pipeline produces a model card stating the model's intended use, tested limits, known failure modes, and retraining envelope. The PMO ISSE checks it against its evidence before certification. Administrator and user documentation for other components comes from their suppliers under their contracts. A system-wide owner is still to be named, and it is tracked as a gap. The SSP describes them under [AI-5.8](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-58-model-card-generation), [AI-6.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-62-model-card-review). |
| SA-8 | Security and Privacy Engineering Principles | System-Specific | Planned | Security engineering principles will be applied as requirements are derived. The PMO ISSE turns the SADD's design principles, such as least privilege, deny by default, and separation of the payload vendor data, into testable requirements for each application. The SSP describes it under [AP-1.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-13-security-requirements-definition). |
| SA-8(33) | Security and Privacy Engineering Principles \| Minimization | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will collect and keep only the personal information its mission needs. Incidental imagery of people is the only personal information in the collection, and training sets keep it only where a detection task requires it. The DMP sets the minimization rules, and the AISP sets the privacy requirements for models. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.9](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-19-data-management-plan-dmp). |
| SA-9 | External System Services | System-Specific | Planned | External services will be held to security requirements through their contracts and authorizations. Azure Government is relied on through its IL5 authorization, which the inherited control check confirms each year. The foundation model runs as a deployment inside KESTREL's own tenant, reached only by private endpoint. Applications call no external service outside the boundary except Purview Information Protection in the Microsoft 365 DoD tenant. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.3](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-33-ai-agent-identities), [AP-2.9](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-29-external-runtime-service-and-client-side-code-governance), [AI-8.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-83-third-partyfoundation-model-api-dependency-governance), [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements), [GV-5.12](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-512-inherited-control-validation). |
| SA-9(2) | External System Services \| Identification of Functions, Ports, Protocols, and Services | System-Specific | Planned | Each external service will identify the functions, ports, protocols, and services it uses, as a clause in the clause library. KESTREL registers each one in the DoD PPSM registry. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-9(5) | External System Services \| Processing, Storage, and Service Location | System-Specific | Planned | Processing and storage will stay in United States regions inside the cloud provider's IL5 authorization. CCSD tailoring action 5 records that location as a parameter, covering the foundation model service and KESTREL's Microsoft 365 DoD tenant. CCSD tailoring action 5 (added) applies. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.9](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-29-external-runtime-service-and-client-side-code-governance), [AI-8.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-83-third-partyfoundation-model-api-dependency-governance). |
| SA-10 | Developer Configuration Management | System-Specific | Planned | Changes to the pipeline itself will be controlled. Every team's pipeline extends the Platform Team's templates, and an unapproved change to a pipeline definition stops the run and alerts the Platform Team and the Security Team. From Phase 2, the templates are signed and verified before each job. Training code and its configuration are versioned and reviewed the same way. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.23](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-223-signedverified-pipeline-definitions), [AI-4.12](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-412-signedverified-training-pipeline-definitions). |
| SA-11 | Developer Testing and Evaluation | System-Specific | Planned | Every application and model will be tested before it is fielded. GitLab DAST scans each candidate application build in stage with a test account for each role. Models are tested for jailbreaks, prompt injection, adversarial evasion, data poisoning, and out-of-distribution inputs, against thresholds the AISP sets for each assurance level. The SSP describes them under [AP-3.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-32-dast), [AI-5.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-51-jailbreak-testing), [AI-5.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-52-prompt-injection-testing), [AI-5.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-53-adversarial-evasion-robustness-testing), [AI-5.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-54-data-poisoning-testing), [AI-5.5](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-55-out-of-distribution-robustness-testing). |
| SA-15 | Development Process, Standards, and Tools | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will set its development processes, standards, and tools in the ASP and the AISP. These cover the threat modeling method, the secure coding standard, the policy-as-code gates, the approved component catalogs, and the model optimization techniques. Both plans are reviewed as a whole each year. The SSP describes them under [AP-1.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-14-application-threat-modeling), [AP-2.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-22-secure-coding-standards-and-build-hardening), [AP-2.19](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-219-policy-as-code-evaluation), [AP-6.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-61-application-security-plan-asp), [AI-1.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-14-approved-ai-component-catalog), [AI-1.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-17-ai-threat-modeling), [AI-3.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-32-experiment-tracking-and-reproducibility), [AI-6.8](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-68-model-optimization-governance), [AI-10.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-101-aiml-security-plan-aisp). |
| SA-15(3) | Development Process, Standards, and Tools \| Criticality Analysis | System-Specific | Planned | A criticality analysis will identify the components and suppliers KESTREL's essential functions depend on. The supply chain lead maps those dependencies each year, flagging single sources and concentrations, and the contract terms for each supplier follow from that analysis. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-16 | Developer-provided Training | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers of critical components to provide training on their security functions, as a clause in the clause library. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-17 | Developer Security and Privacy Architecture and Design | System-Specific | Planned | Each application's security architecture will follow the SADD's design, and its threat model will document how the application meets it. The PMO ISSE checks both at the design gate before building starts. The SSP describes it under [AP-1.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-13-security-requirements-definition). |
| SA-21 | Developer Screening | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to screen the developers who work on KESTREL's components, as a clause in the clause library. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-22 | Unsupported System Components | System-Specific | Planned | Each asset's end of support will be forecast at least 12 months ahead, so it can be replaced in time. An asset kept past its end of support needs an exception, with its compensating controls and a replacement date. The payload processing workstation is the known case, replaced by 2027-09-30, and it connects only if the AO re-dates CCSD tailoring action 3. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-23-resource-decommissioning-governance). |

### SC: System and Communications Protection

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SC-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the system and communications protection policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Key Management Plan will hold the cryptographic procedures, and the CMP the network and boundary procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve them, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DA-3.13](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-313-key-management-plan-kmp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| SC-2 | Separation of System and User Functionality | System-Specific | Planned | Administration will be kept apart from user functions. Tier 0 is administered only from physical privileged access workstations, and Tier 1 from the Platform Team's own Azure Virtual Desktop host pool, never from a user desktop. Administrators hold separate accounts for administrative work. The VDI brokers have their own listener and subnet, apart from user-facing applications. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-42-privileged-access-workstations-and-administrative-tiering), [NE-2.13](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-213-authorized-cloud-access-point-integration). |
| SC-3 | Security Function Isolation | System-Specific | Planned | Virtualization-based security will isolate the EDR agent and the credential stores on every workstation, desktop, and Windows server. Tamper protection, owned by the Tier 0 administrators and changed only with the Security Team's approval, keeps the EDR agent itself from being switched off. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-53-host-hardening-and-integrity-protection). |
| SC-4 | Information in Shared System Resources | Hybrid | Planned | Information will not carry over between users of shared resources. Each training run gets its own containers, and its scratch storage is destroyed when it ends, so cached data and tensors cannot reach the next job. Pipeline jobs run on fresh runner pods that are destroyed afterward. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Isolation of shared hardware through the isolated VM sizes IL5 requires. The SSP describes it under [AI-4.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-41-ephemeral-containerized-training-environments). |
| SC-5 | Denial-of-service Protection | Hybrid | Planned | Network-layer floods will be absorbed upstream by DISA's internet access points and the Boundary Cloud Access Point, since the DMZ holds no cloud public addresses. Application Gateway limits the request rate to each user-facing application, and API Management limits each partner and each caller of the model endpoints. DoS protection policies on the cloud hub limit what any one spoke can send. Flood alerts go to Splunk. **Inherited from DISA:** Network-layer flood absorption at the internet access points and the Boundary Cloud Access Point. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.5](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-25-ddos-protection), [NE-2.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-26-web-application-firewall), [AI-8.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-82-api-abuse-protection). |
| SC-7 | Boundary Protection | Hybrid | Planned | KESTREL's external boundary will be the Boundary Cloud Access Point and the cloud hub, with the data center hub as the managed interface for its own external links. Internal boundaries divide the cloud's ten spokes, the data center's SDN segments, and the ground segment's IEC 62443 zones. Each ground segment zone joins the IT network only through its conduit. Platform services add their own resource firewalls, admitting only their spoke's private endpoint. **Inherited from DISA:** Boundary protection at the Boundary Cloud Access Point. The SSP describes them under [NE-1.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-14-network-macro-segmentation), [NE-1.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-16-itot-zone-and-conduit-segmentation-iec-62443), [NE-2.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-23-service-native-firewall-configurations). |
| SC-7(3) | Boundary Protection \| Access Points | System-Specific | Planned | External connections will be limited to a small set of managed access points. All user traffic arrives through the Boundary Cloud Access Point and the cloud hub. Outbound traffic leaves only through the hubs, and only for an allow-list of named classes. These are package sources, PKI revocation, the time reference, the threat feed, the Microsoft 365 DoD tenant, and the paging service. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-24-network-firewall). |
| SC-7(4) | Boundary Protection \| External Telecommunications Services | Hybrid | Planned | Each external telecommunications service will have a managed interface. The three dedicated circuits ride DISN through the Boundary Cloud Access Point and terminate on the cloud hub and each site's firewall. Their traffic runs inside IPsec tunnels between the firewalls. BGP sessions are authenticated, and prefix filters accept only KESTREL's address ranges. Every port, protocol, and service crossing them is registered in the DoD PPSM registry with its justification. **Inherited from DISA:** Managed external telecommunications through the Boundary Cloud Access Point. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.1](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-21-private-connectivity), [NE-2.13](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-213-authorized-cloud-access-point-integration). |
| SC-7(5) | Boundary Protection \| Deny by Default — Allow by Exception | System-Specific | Planned | Every boundary will deny traffic by default and allow it by exception. Workload security groups, ACI contracts, Cilium network policies, and the ground segment conduits each allow only mapped flows. Training compute reaches only the model registry, the package mirror, and the training data zone. The SSP describes them under [NE-1.5](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-15-network-micro-segmentation), [NE-1.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-16-itot-zone-and-conduit-segmentation-iec-62443), [AP-2.17](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-217-network-policy-verification), [AI-4.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-43-training-cluster-network-segmentation-and-egress-control). |
| SC-7(7) | Boundary Protection \| Split Tunneling for Remote Devices | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL offers no network tunnel to any remote user. Remote access runs through Pomerium or Azure Virtual Desktop, and neither routes the user's device onto KESTREL's network, so split tunneling cannot occur. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-27-secure-remote-access). |
| SC-7(8) | Boundary Protection \| Route Traffic to Authenticated Proxy Servers | System-Specific | Planned | Outbound traffic will pass through the hubs' firewalls, which decrypt and inspect TLS and apply URL filtering. Remote users reach applications only through Pomerium, the identity-aware proxy, or the VDI brokers, both of which authenticate the user first. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-24-network-firewall), [NE-2.13](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-213-authorized-cloud-access-point-integration). |
| SC-7(18) | Boundary Protection \| Fail Secure | System-Specific | Planned | Boundary devices will fail to a safe state. The firewalls, the access proxy, the VDI brokers, and the cross domain transfer gateway fail closed. On the ground segment, a deep packet inspection fault falls back to a fixed allow-list of each station's approved commands. Launch and recovery keep working, and nothing new is allowed. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.11](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-211-industrial-protocol-filtering-dpi). |
| SC-7(21) | Boundary Protection \| Isolation of System Components | System-Specific | Planned | The components with the most risk will each sit in their own segment. The DMZ, the VDI spoke, and Tier 0 are isolated, and so is each ground segment zone. Each Key Vault is reachable only through its own spoke's private endpoint. The SSP describes them under [NE-1.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-14-network-macro-segmentation), [NE-1.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-16-itot-zone-and-conduit-segmentation-iec-62443), [DA-3.11](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-311-secrets-vault-network-security-hardening). |
| SC-7(24) | Boundary Protection \| Personally Identifiable Information | System-Specific | Planned | Data loss prevention will watch personal information at the boundary. The partner API and the cross domain transfer gateway check every release against its markings, and the DMP's rules block personal information on each named outbound path. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.5](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-15-data-loss-prevention-dlp-and-monitoring). |
| SC-8 | Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity | System-Specific | Planned | Data in transit will be protected for confidentiality and integrity. Every connection uses TLS 1.2 or later, and services authenticate each other with mutual TLS using program PKI certificates. Traffic across the dedicated circuits runs inside IPsec tunnels. The aircraft datalinks use authenticated encryption on FIPS 140-3 validated crypto modules. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.8](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-28-telemetry-tracking-and-command-ttc-link-security), [DA-2.2](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-22-tls-encryption-enforcement), [DA-2.3](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-23-secure-file-transfer-and-management-protocols). |
| SC-8(1) | Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity \| Cryptographic Protection | System-Specific | Planned | The protection in transit will be cryptographic, using FIPS 140-3 validated modules and CNSA algorithms. The IPsec tunnels run in FIPS-CC mode, and the datalinks use CNSA algorithms under CNSSP 15. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.8](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-28-telemetry-tracking-and-command-ttc-link-security), [DA-2.2](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-22-tls-encryption-enforcement), [DA-2.3](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-23-secure-file-transfer-and-management-protocols). |
| SC-10 | Network Disconnect | System-Specific | Planned | Remote sessions will end after 15 idle minutes, and the Security Team can end any session at once. Cloud and VDI sessions also follow the AMP's limits under continuous access evaluation. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-27-secure-remote-access). |
| SC-12 | Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management | System-Specific | Planned | Keys will be generated, stored, and managed under the Key Management Plan. The root keys sit in the nShield HSMs in the data center, under KESTREL's own security world. Each spoke's customer-managed keys are generated in the HSMs and imported into Azure Key Vault Premium, which holds them at FIPS 140-3 Level 3. Key Vault rotates its keys on the KMP's schedule, and imported keys are replaced by an HSM job before they expire. Key administration is separated from key use. The SSP describes them under [DA-2.5](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-25-encryption-key-ownership-and-control), [DA-3.3](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-33-key-management-policies-and-infrastructure), [DA-3.5](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-35-key-lifecycle-automation). |
| SC-12(1) | Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management \| Availability | System-Specific | Planned | Keys whose loss would destroy data will stay available. Backup set keys and other such keys are escrowed in the alternate site's HSM under split knowledge. Recovering one needs two of the four administrator cards. The SSP describes it under [DA-3.5](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-35-key-lifecycle-automation). |
| SC-13 | Cryptographic Protection | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will use only FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules and CNSA algorithms. AES-256 protects data at rest. The datalink crypto modules and the HSMs are validated, and so is the cloud's Key Vault Premium. The SSP describes it under [DA-3.1](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-31-fips-140--approved-cryptographic-module-baseline). |
| SC-15 | Collaborative Computing Devices and Applications | System-Specific | Planned | Cameras and microphones will be disabled on the privileged access workstations and in the VDI image, so no collaborative device can be switched on remotely. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| SC-17 | Public Key Infrastructure Certificates | Hybrid | Planned | Certificates will come from approved authorities. The program PKI issues device, workload, and service certificates from issuing authorities under an offline root whose key is held in the HSMs. Keyfactor Command tracks every certificate. User-facing edge services present DoD PKI server certificates that browsers and partner systems already trust. **Inherited from DoD PKI:** DoD PKI server certificates for user-facing edge services. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-34-server-and-services-authentication), [DA-3.7](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-37-certificate-policies-and-integration), [DA-3.9](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-39-certificate-lifecycle-and-revocation). |
| SC-18 | Mobile Code | System-Specific | Planned | Allow-listing will block unapproved code, including scripts, on every workstation, desktop, and server. Attack surface reduction rules on Windows hosts block scripts and macros from untrusted sources. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| SC-20 | Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Authoritative Source) | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL's public names will sit under the program's DoD parent zone, signed with DNSSEC. DoD publishes their delegation records, and the names point only at the access point's published addresses. The SSP describes it under [NE-3.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-33-trusted-dns-service). |
| SC-21 | Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver) | System-Specific | Planned | Every KESTREL resolver will validate DNSSEC on the answers it returns. Hosts may use no other resolver, and the hubs block outbound DNS to anywhere else. The SSP describes it under [NE-3.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-33-trusted-dns-service). |
| SC-22 | Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service | System-Specific | Planned | Name resolution will be redundant and split by role. Infoblox appliances serve the data center and the alternate site, and virtual appliances serve the cloud from Platform Prod. Each operating site has its own resolver pair. No KESTREL resolver answers for the public names, so the authoritative and recursive roles stay separate. The SSP describes them under [NE-3.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-33-trusted-dns-service), [NE-3.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-34-private-dns-service). |
| SC-23 | Session Authenticity | System-Specific | Planned | Session authenticity will be protected by TLS on every session and by short-lived, signed tokens. Continuous access evaluation revokes a session's tokens when the account is disabled or its risk becomes severe. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-26-continuous-authentication). |
| SC-24 | Fail in Known State | System-Specific | Planned | The firewalls, the access proxy, the VDI brokers, and the cross domain transfer gateway will fail closed. Each preserves its state so it can recover to a known configuration. The SSP describes it under [DI-3.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-31-secure-configurations). |
| SC-28 | Protection of Information at Rest | System-Specific | Planned | Information at rest will be protected in every store. Each data lake zone, database, and storage service is encrypted, and backups and audit logs sit in immutable storage that no account can alter before its retention ends. The SSP describes it under [DA-2.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-24-default-data-at-rest-encryption). |
| SC-28(1) | Protection of Information at Rest \| Cryptographic Protection | System-Specific | Planned | Every store will be encrypted with AES-256 under keys KESTREL controls, as the DMP sets for each label. Each data lake zone uses its own key, personal fields use column encryption, and model artifacts are encrypted in the registry and on serving nodes. Edge models are encrypted under a key rooted in the HSMs. Reports released to partners are wrapped with Purview Information Protection. The SSP describes them under [AI-8.11](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-811-model-artifact-encryption-and-watermarking), [DA-1.6](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-16-data-rights-management-drm), [DA-2.1](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-21-classification-tied-documentfield-level-encryption), [DA-2.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-24-default-data-at-rest-encryption). |
| SC-39 | Process Isolation | System-Specific | Planned | Each process that handles untrusted or sensitive work will run in its own isolated environment. Every pipeline job runs on a fresh runner pod, every training run in its own containers, and every model evaluation in a disposable environment. Each AI agent tool runs in its own Container Instances group with hypervisor isolation. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.21](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-221-ephemeralisolated-build-environments), [AI-3.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-31-secure-experimentation-environment), [AI-4.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-41-ephemeral-containerized-training-environments), [AI-7.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-73-secure-model-evaluation-environment), [AI-8.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-87-agentic-tool-callaction-output-validation). |

### SI: System and Information Integrity

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SI-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the system and information integrity policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Vulnerability and Patch Management Plan will hold the flaw remediation procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DI-7.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-71-vulnerability-and-patch-management-plan-vpmp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| SI-2 | Flaw Remediation | System-Specific | Planned | Flaws will be found and fixed on the VPMP's deadlines, which are shorter for the DMZ, Tier 0, and the fleet. ACAS scans every host from Phase 1, and Dependency-Track checks every fielded release's SBOM daily. Patches move through dev, test, and stage before production, and container images are rebuilt rather than patched. Fleet patches must be validated by the manufacturer and tried on a spare. CCSD tailoring action 3 (compensating control) applies, approved by the AO with conditions. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.8](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-48-vulnerability-and-patch-management), [AP-5.12](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-512-fielded-dependency-vulnerability-monitoring). |
| SI-2(2) | Flaw Remediation \| Automated Flaw Remediation Status | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk and Jira Service Management will track every finding's remediation status automatically against its deadline, and report findings past their deadline in each continuous monitoring cycle. The SSP describes it under [DI-4.8](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-48-vulnerability-and-patch-management). |
| SI-3 | Malicious Code Protection | System-Specific | Planned | Malicious code protection will run at every entry point. Defender for Endpoint runs on every server, workstation, and VDI desktop, and Defender for Containers protects every cluster. ClamAV scans every package and image the mirror fetches and every build artifact. ModelScan checks every model file before it can load. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-52-malicious-code-protection), [AP-2.6](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-26-malware-scanning), [AI-4.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-47-model-artifact-malwareunsafe-deserialization-scanning). |
| SI-4 | System Monitoring | Hybrid | Planned | KESTREL will monitor itself in every location. Splunk Enterprise Security correlates telemetry from endpoints, identity, the network, the cloud, data services, the models, and the ground segment. The CSSP monitors the same telemetry around the clock under its service agreement. Monitoring is tightened after an incident and around any asset that cannot be patched. **Inherited from the CSSP:** Around-the-clock monitoring of forwarded telemetry. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-35-secrets-and-credentials-detection), [DI-4.9](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-49-unpatchablelegacy-asset-compensating-controls), [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection), [NE-3.1](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-31-network-telemetry-and-security-posture-visualization), [NE-3.5](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-35-dns-advanced-protection), [AI-3.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-34-training-script-and-feature-engineering-ip-protection), [AI-7.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-74-continuous-authentication-of-feedbackretraining-data), [AI-8.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-81-extraction-abuse-monitoring), [AI-9.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-91-model-drift-detection-and-alerting), [AI-9.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-92-data-drift-detection-and-alerting), [DA-1.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-14-database-and-storage-threat-detection), [DA-3.12](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-312-secrets-vault-protection-and-monitoring), [DE-1.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-11-platform-native-threat-detection), [RS-3.6](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-36-recovery-and-return-to-operations-validation). |
| SI-4(2) | System Monitoring \| Automated Tools and Mechanisms for Real-time Analysis | System-Specific | Planned | Monitoring will use automated tools for real-time analysis. These are Defender for Cloud and Defender for Identity for their services, Defender for Endpoint on hosts, and Splunk Enterprise Security correlation across them. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-14-identity-platform-threat-detection-and-hardening), [ID-1.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-16-third-party-application-and-saas-access-governance), [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection), [DA-1.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-14-database-and-storage-threat-detection), [DE-1.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-11-platform-native-threat-detection). |
| SI-4(4) | System Monitoring \| Inbound and Outbound Communications Traffic | System-Specific | Planned | Inbound and outbound traffic will be monitored at the hubs and at each ground segment conduit. On the conduit, the firewall parses the command and control protocol and blocks any command a station is not approved to send. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.11](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-211-industrial-protocol-filtering-dpi). |
| SI-4(5) | System Monitoring \| System-generated Alerts | System-Specific | Planned | Systems will raise alerts when indicators of compromise appear. These include EDR detections, sign-in risk, unusual data access, deviations on the ground segment, and spoofing or jamming of navigation signals. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection), [NE-3.8](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-38-otlegacy-passive-monitoring), [NE-3.9](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-39-gnsspnt-spoofing-and-jamming-detection), [DA-1.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-14-database-and-storage-threat-detection), [DE-1.8](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-18-identity-threat-detection). |
| SI-4(10) | System Monitoring \| Visibility of Encrypted Communications | System-Specific | Planned | Both hubs will decrypt outbound TLS for inspection. Mutual TLS between workload identities is exempt, since decrypting it would break the identity it carries. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-24-network-firewall). |
| SI-4(12) | System Monitoring \| Automated Organization-generated Alerts | System-Specific | Planned | Splunk will alert the Security Team automatically on events that need attention, such as model-serving abuse that spans several endpoints. The SSP describes them under [AI-9.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-94-production-abuse-monitoring), [DE-3.1](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-31-siem-capabilities). |
| SI-4(14) | System Monitoring \| Wireless Intrusion Detection | System-Specific | Planned | From Phase 2, Bastille sensors will detect rogue access points and unauthorized radios at the data center and the alternate site. They extend to each operating site in Phase 3. The SSP describes it under [NE-1.8](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-18-wireless-network-access-control). |
| SI-4(20) | System Monitoring \| Privileged Users | System-Specific | Planned | CyberArk will record every privileged session and let reviewers watch it live and end it. User activity monitoring covers privileged users in particular. The SSP describes it under [ID-4.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-44-privileged-credential-vaulting-and-session-brokering). |
| SI-4(22) | System Monitoring \| Unauthorized Network Services | System-Specific | Planned | The pipeline will compare observed reachability with the registered ports, protocols, and services on every change, so an unauthorized network service is found. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.12](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-212-ports-protocols-and-services-matrix-ppsm). |
| SI-5 | Security Alerts, Advisories, and Directives | System-Specific | Planned | The Security Team will receive security alerts and directives, such as IAVM notices and CYBERCOM tasking orders, through the CSSP. Each directive opens a Jira ticket, and its remediation is tracked against the directive's own compliance date. The CSSP's indicators arrive with a confidence tier and an expiry. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.8](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-48-vulnerability-and-patch-management), [DE-1.3](../06-ssp/08-detection.md#de-13-correlated-threat-detection-and-analytics). |
| SI-5(1) | Security Alerts, Advisories, and Directives \| Automated Alerts and Advisories | System-Specific | Planned | Advisories and indicators from the CSSP will arrive automatically, as STIX over TAXII. The SSP describes it under [RS-1.7](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-17-cyber-defense-service-provider-alignment). |
| SI-6 | Security and Privacy Function Verification | System-Specific | Planned | Security functions will be checked to confirm they still work. Boot integrity attestation and file integrity monitoring verify hosts, and canary prompts with known answers run daily against every fielded model to confirm its guardrails have not changed. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection), [AI-9.5](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-95-canary-prompt-testing). |
| SI-7 | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity | System-Specific | Planned | Software and information will be protected against unauthorized change. Tamper protection keeps the EDR agent running, and exploit protection guards every host. The applications serve only their own client code, with content security policies blocking anything else. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-53-host-hardening-and-integrity-protection), [AP-2.9](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-29-external-runtime-service-and-client-side-code-governance). |
| SI-7(1) | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity \| Integrity Checks | System-Specific | Planned | Integrity checks will run wherever a change would matter. File integrity monitoring covers Tier 0, and training environments check their own hashes before each run. Training data, recalled agent memory, and retrieved documents are checked before they are used. The retraining pipeline is compared with its certified version each week. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection), [AI-2.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-21-data-poisoning-prevention-and-detection), [AI-4.13](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-413-reproducibility-controls), [AI-7.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-72-retraining-data-integrity-checks), [AI-8.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-84-retrieval-augmented-generation-rag-and-vector-store-security), [AI-8.15](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-815-agent-memory-security), [AI-9.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-93-retraining-pipeline-integrity-verification). |
| SI-7(2) | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity \| Automated Notifications of Integrity Violations | System-Specific | Planned | File integrity monitoring will alert the Security Team on any integrity violation it finds. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection). |
| SI-7(5) | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity \| Automated Response to Integrity Violations | System-Specific | Planned | An integrity violation will trigger an automatic response where it is safe to do so. A training batch that fails its screens is blocked from the training zone, and a host that fails integrity checks is flagged for response. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection), [AI-2.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-21-data-poisoning-prevention-and-detection). |
| SI-7(7) | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity \| Integration of Detection and Response | System-Specific | Planned | Integrity violations will feed incident response directly, raising alerts in Splunk that open incident records under the IRP. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-54-endpoint-detection). |
| SI-7(15) | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity \| Code Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Code will be authenticated before it is installed or run. Release images and packages are signed with Cosign, and only signed images with a Certification to Field attestation are admitted to production. Pretrained checkpoints are checked against their publisher's signature or digest, and reference and trained models are signed. Firmware is verified against its manufacturer's signature or published hash. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.13](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-213-image-signing), [AI-1.5](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-15-model-provenance-and-integrity-verification), [AI-3.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-33-signedhashed-reference-models), [AI-4.14](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-414-training-artifact-signing), [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
| SI-8 | Spam Protection | Removed | Removed | CCSD tailoring action 1 removed it. |
| SI-8(2) | Spam Protection \| Automatic Updates | Removed | Removed | CCSD tailoring action 1 removed it with its base control. |
| SI-10 | Information Input Validation | System-Specific | Planned | Inputs will be validated before they are used. The WAF and API Management check each request against its schema, and the model endpoints check type, size, and format before LLM Guard screens prompts for injection. Training labels and retraining records are validated for schema, ranges, and floods. The SSP describes them under [ID-2.3](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-23-single-sign-on-sso), [NE-2.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-26-web-application-firewall), [AP-3.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-34-api-security-testing), [AI-2.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-22-label-integrity-verification), [AI-7.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-72-retraining-data-integrity-checks), [AI-8.5](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-85-input-validation). |
| SI-11 | Error Handling | System-Specific | Planned | Applications will show users a generic error and send diagnostic detail only to logs that authorized staff can read. The SSP describes it under [AP-2.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-22-secure-coding-standards-and-build-hardening). |
| SI-12 | Information Management and Retention | System-Specific | Planned | Information will be kept only as long as the DMP's retention schedule allows, then disposed of as it sets out. Registry images and model versions expire on the ASP's and the AISP's schedules, and agent memory entries expire after 180 days. Evidence is kept in immutable storage for as long as its rules require. The SSP describes them under [AP-5.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-54-registry-hygiene-report), [AI-8.15](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-815-agent-memory-security), [AI-9.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-97-model-registry-hygiene-report), [DA-1.9](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-19-data-management-plan-dmp), [CO-1.3](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-13-compliance-evidence-collection-and-retention). |
| SI-12(1) | Information Management and Retention \| Limit Personally Identifiable Information Elements | System-Specific | Planned | Personal information will be limited to what each purpose needs. Presidio redacts personal information from inference logs, and the DMP's minimization rules cover every other record. The SSP describes them under [AI-8.8](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-88-inference-time-pii-handling), [DA-1.9](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-19-data-management-plan-dmp). |
| SI-12(2) | Information Management and Retention \| Minimize Personally Identifiable Information in Testing, Training, and Research | System-Specific | Planned | Test, training, and research data will hold no identifying text, and no imagery of people unless the AISP's privacy requirements allow it. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.9](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-19-data-management-plan-dmp). |
| SI-12(3) | Information Management and Retention \| Information Disposal | System-Specific | Planned | Information will be disposed of with the method the DMP sets for each kind. Drives are purged on site with Blancco, HSMs are zeroized, and cloud media is sanitized by the provider. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.8](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-18-media-protection-policy-and-procedures). |
| SI-16 | Memory Protection | System-Specific | Planned | Memory will be protected from unauthorized code execution. Exploit protection applies data execution prevention and address space randomization on every host, and virtualization-based security isolates credential stores. The pipeline applies compiler hardening settings to every build. The SSP describes them under [DI-5.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-53-host-hardening-and-integrity-protection), [AP-2.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-22-secure-coding-standards-and-build-hardening). |
| SI-18 | Personally Identifiable Information Quality Operations | System-Specific | Planned | The Privacy Impact Assessment will set how the accuracy of personal information is maintained. Account records are synchronized against the authoritative source. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-41-privacy-program-management). |
| SI-18(4) | Personally Identifiable Information Quality Operations \| Individual Requests | System-Specific | Planned | The privacy officer will handle requests from individuals to correct their personal information. The SSP describes it under [CO-4.1](../06-ssp/13-compliance.md#co-41-privacy-program-management). |
| SI-19 | De-identification | System-Specific | Planned | Personal information will be removed or masked before data is used for testing, training, or release. Presidio removes identifying text, and people in imagery are blurred or cropped, by a Data Team reviewer until the person-detection model is certified. The privacy officer approves each technique. The SSP describes them under [AI-1.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-12-privacy-requirements-definition), [AI-2.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-23-training-data-privacy-controls), [AI-8.8](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-88-inference-time-pii-handling), [DA-1.7](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-17-dataset-de-identification-and-disclosure-review). |

### SR: Supply Chain Risk Management

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SR-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the supply chain risk management policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Supply Chain Risk Management Plan will hold the procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework), [GV-3.5](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-35-supply-chain-risk-management-plan-scrm). |
| SR-2 | Supply Chain Risk Management Plan | System-Specific | Planned | The supply chain lead will write the Supply Chain Risk Management Plan with the SCRM team. It covers vendor assessment and tiering, contract security requirements, the supply chain risk assessment and dependency map, sourcing and inspection, and component disposal. The ISSM and the PMO ISSE review it, the Configuration Control Board approves it, and it is revised each year and whenever a Tier 1 supplier changes. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.5](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-35-supply-chain-risk-management-plan-scrm). |
| SR-2(1) | Supply Chain Risk Management Plan \| Establish SCRM Team | System-Specific | Planned | A standing SCRM team, chaired by the supply chain lead, will meet each month and whenever a Tier 1 supplier changes. Its members include the contracting officer, program legal counsel, the PMO ISSE, the ISSM, and the leads who receive hardware for the data center and the fleet. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.5](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-35-supply-chain-risk-management-plan-scrm). |
| SR-3 | Supply Chain Controls and Processes | System-Specific | Planned | Components will enter KESTREL only through controlled paths. Builds resolve packages only through Artifactory, which draws each ecosystem from its approved upstream. Every dependency change is reviewed for vulnerabilities, license terms, and package health before it can merge. Every software supplier delivers an SBOM with each release, which is loaded into Dependency-Track and monitored for new flaws. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.7](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-27-trusted-internal-package-repository), [AP-2.8](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-28-dependency-review), [AP-2.12](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-212-vendor-sbom-intake), [GV-3.3](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-33-supply-chain-risk-assessment-and-dependency-mapping). |
| SR-5 | Acquisition Strategies, Tools, and Methods | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will buy hardware only from manufacturers and authorized resellers, and its contracts will carry clause sets matched to each supplier's risk. Sole-source or obsolete parts bought elsewhere need the SCRM team's approval, a stricter inspection, and a risk acceptance. The SSP describes them under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements), [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
| SR-6 | Supplier Assessments and Reviews | System-Specific | Planned | Every commercial supplier will answer KESTREL's security questionnaire before contract award, including questions on ownership and foreign influence. Suppliers are tiered by what they can reach, and Tier 1 suppliers are reassessed every year. Model publishers, dataset sources, and the foundation model provider are assessed against the AISP's criteria as well. The SSP describes them under [AI-1.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-13-model-selection-and-justification), [AI-2.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-22-label-integrity-verification), [AI-8.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-83-third-partyfoundation-model-api-dependency-governance), [GV-3.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-31-vendor-security-risk-assessment). |
| SR-8 | Notification Agreements | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to notify KESTREL of a compromise or a failed audit, as a clause in the clause library's software and Tier 1 clause sets. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SR-9 | Tamper Resistance and Detection | System-Specific | Planned | Hardware will be inspected for tampering when it arrives and again when it returns from vendor service. Inspectors check packaging and seals, markings, serial and lot numbers, and physical characteristics against a known-good unit. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
| SR-9(1) | Tamper Resistance and Detection \| Multiple Stages of System Development Life Cycle | System-Specific | Planned | Tamper resistance and detection will apply at more than one stage of the lifecycle. Suppliers' own controls are assessed before award, hardware is inspected at receipt and after service, and stations and avionics are rescanned each year. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
| SR-10 | Inspection of Systems or Components | System-Specific | Planned | The Platform Team will inspect data center hardware at receipt from Phase 1, and Fleet Operations will inspect fleet equipment from Phase 3. Each item is also inspected again when it returns from vendor service. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
| SR-11 | Component Authenticity | System-Specific | Planned | Firmware will come only from the manufacturer or its authorized channel, and its signature will be verified before installation. Unsigned firmware is checked against the manufacturer's published hash. Each verified version is recorded against its device in Jira Service Management Assets. A suspect counterfeit part is quarantined and reported to its source, to GIDEP, to the contracting officer, and to the ISSM. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
| SR-11(1) | Component Authenticity \| Anti-counterfeit Training | System-Specific | Planned | The staff who receive and inspect hardware, in the Platform Team and Fleet Operations, will be trained to recognize counterfeit indicators. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
| SR-11(2) | Component Authenticity \| Configuration Control for Component Service and Repair | System-Specific | Planned | Components sent out for service or repair will be inspected again when they return, before they are reinstalled, and their firmware is verified as on first receipt. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
| SR-11(3) | Component Authenticity \| Anti-counterfeit Scanning | System-Specific | Planned | Ground control stations and aircraft avionics will be rescanned for counterfeit parts each year, at a maintenance window, focusing on parts that entered through vendor service channels. CCSD tailoring action 4 added this control. CCSD tailoring action 4 (added) applies. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
| SR-12 | Component Disposal | System-Specific | Planned | Retired components will be disposed of so that nobody can recover them. Drives are purged on site with Blancco to NIST SP 800-88, verified, and shredded. HSMs and datalink crypto modules are zeroized and then destroyed. A retired model's weights and derived embeddings are deleted, and its copies are removed from every aircraft. Each disposal is recorded with its method and a certificate of destruction. The SSP describes them under [AI-9.8](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-98-model-decommissioning-and-disposal), [GV-3.4](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-34-hardware-and-firmware-provenance-verification). |
